# gh-1438: [WIP][GOAL] bash_job id-churn hardening — near-miss resolution, bounded status, exited-job GC

## Description

## Goal — bash_job id-churn hardening (v2, repair edit: mechanism + amplification + retracted framings + threat model + E2E layer; line numbers re-pinned)

One sentence: **`bash_job` becomes forgiving of stale and near-miss job ids** — an unknown id resolves to its closest retained job instead of dead-ending, and the tool's outputs stay bounded.

Observed in production (chief session, ~13h of monitor shifts): the agent re-polled job ids reconstructed from memory (correct `sh-NNNN-` numeric part, wrong hash suffix) — every poll returned a bare `unknown background job` error with zero recovery information, so the poll-per-turn loop survived for hundreds of turns. Separately, `bash_job status` with no id dumped 1600+ lines of exited jobs into the agent context.

## Why this framing

- ~~"Agent discipline problem — fix via prompt."~~ **RETRACTED.** The harness must be robust to imperfect id recall; a prompt-side "don't poll stale ids" fix depends on exactly the faculty that failed (memory reconstruction across hundreds of turns).
- ~~"Registry reaps finished jobs while notices still reference them."~~ **RETRACTED by evidence:** `_jobs` is grow-only — all ~1600 exited jobs were retained with their logs; the polled ids were **near-misses** (correct `sh-NNNN-` numeric part, wrong hash suffix), never reaped ids.
- ~~"Deduplicate settle notices."~~ **RETRACTED:** the notice path already carries suppression (`suppressSettleNotification`, lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:119; call site builtin_tools_bash.dart:490 — #562 shipped it). The loop was **poll-side**, not notice-side.

### Mechanism (falsifiable, step-1 form)

Settle wake arrives with the job id as free text → the agent answers `bash_job(output)` with an id reconstructed from memory → `job(id)` is an exact-match lookup over retained entries (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:215), so a one-char-wrong id is **indistinguishable from one that never existed** → the verb dead-ends in `StateError('unknown background job: $id')` (builtin_tools_bash.dart:586 / :606, shell_jobs.dart:300) with **zero recovery signal** — no near-miss candidates, no "exited Nm ago", no log-dir hint → each settle wake re-arms the same wrong poll.

### Why it survived ~13h / hundreds of turns (amplification)

The dead-end error is terminal and information-free: nothing in the result tells the agent to stop, re-derive, or look in `.fah/bash_jobs/`, so nothing breaks the loop from the tool side. Every iteration is answered with a competent one-line "routine" reply, which masks the loop in the transcript as normal task discharge — hours of successful-looking execution outweigh any lost instruction (self-precedent). And the agent's periodic no-id `bash_job status` flooded context with 1600+ exited-job status lines (observed live), burying the correct id under noise and further degrading id fidelity on the next reconstruction.

## Pinned facts (current code — verified against the working tree, this edit)

- `ShellJobRegistry._jobs` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:199) is a grow-only list — exited jobs are retained for the process lifetime with their logs; there is no GC and no cap. (pos: AC3 bounding holds over 0/100/10k retained; neg: current unbounded dump is the REG baseline)
- Exact-match lookup `ShellJobEntry? job(String id)` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:215) returns null on any mismatch. (pos: AC1 near-miss resolution; neg: E3 non-`sh-NNNN-` shape skips resolution)
- Unknown ids throw `StateError('unknown background job: $id')` from three verb paths: builtin_tools_bash.dart:586 (`status`), :606 (`stop`), shell_jobs.dart:300 (`tail`, used by `output`). (pos: AC2 non-error recovery result; neg: E2 clean error after GC+log deletion)
- `tail()` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:297) reads the job's log file raw. (pos: AC1 resolved tail; neg: E2 deleted-log degradation)
- `_bashJobStatusResult` (builtin_tools_bash.dart:576) with no id maps every retained entry 1:1 via `jobs.jobs.map(_shellJobStatusLine).join('\n')` — unbounded by construction. (pos: AC3 bounded rendering; neg: `all: true` opt-out still restores the full dump)
- Logs persist under `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log` and remain readable after exit; on-disk content is NOT redacted (see threat model).
- Retraction evidence: notice suppression exists — `suppressSettleNotification` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:119, called at builtin_tools_bash.dart:490).

## Capability surface (bash_job call shapes → behavior)

| call | today | becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `output`/`status` exact id, live or exited | works (tail from log) | unchanged, plus "exited Nm ago" context |
| `output` unknown id, unique `sh-NNNN-` prefix match among retained jobs | error dead-end | resolve: return that job's tail + corrected id + "already exited — stop polling the stale id" |
| `output`/`status` unknown id, ambiguous or no match | bare error | plain result listing up to 3 closest retained ids + "this id was never registered; do not retry" |
| `stop` unknown id | error dead-end | same closest-ids hint, but **never resolves**: destructive actions require the exact id |
| `status` no id | full dump (unbounded) | running jobs in full + last 20 exited + counts; `all: true` restores the full dump |
| registry growth | unbounded | **second tier**: cap retained exited entries (config, LRU by settle time; logs stay on disk); post-GC exact-id `output` falls back to the on-disk log |

**Invariant: resolution is read-only.** `output`/`status` may act on a resolved near-miss; `stop` never kills a guessed id.

**Tiering:** rows 1–5 are **core** (this card); registry GC is **second tier** (opt-in config, follow-up friendly); the excluded list below is **excluded** with rationale.

### Security threat model

- **Attacker-controlled inputs:** job **command strings** and **log content**. Logs are written to `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log` and read back **raw** by `tail()` — on-disk bytes are NOT redacted — and both flow into `status` lines and `output` tails. Resolution therefore must not surface MORE attacker-controlled text than today's exact-id path: same tail budget, same `_shellJobStatusLine` shape. Resolution changes routing, not volume.
- **Id-enumeration side-channel:** the ≤3 closest-ids candidate list is a minor enumeration aid. Job ids are session-local and not secrets — accepted risk, stated here rather than hidden; no rate-limiting.
- **Instruction hierarchy / destructive gate:** a typo'd or prompt-injected `bash_job stop` must never kill a job the caller did not name exactly. `stop` never acts on a resolved id (AC5) — only the exact id authorizes a destructive verb; resolution is hygiene, the exact-id requirement is the boundary.
- **Impossible by construction:** resolution never fabricates log content — it returns `tail()` of a retained entry's real file, or the same clean error as today (E2).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — `output` with a near-miss id (same `sh-NNNN-` prefix, wrong suffix, exactly one retained match) returns the resolved job's tail, names the corrected id, and states it already exited. (IT, fake registry/env; E2E-1)
- **AC2** — unresolvable unknown id returns a NON-error result with ≤3 closest ids and an explicit do-not-retry note. (IT)
- **AC3** — `status` no-id output line count = running + min(exited, 20) + summary, verified as a property over registries with 0/100/10k exited jobs. (UT/IT; E2E-2)
- **AC4** — after GC prunes an exited entry, exact-id `output` still returns the tail from the on-disk log while the log exists; deleted log degrades to today's clean error. (IT)
- **AC5** — `stop` never acts on a resolved near-miss id (asserted: no kill call, hint returned). (IT)

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, layered UT/IT/E2E/REG

- `UT-*` pure id-distance/prefix resolution + status-bounding math (AC1/AC3).
- `IT-*` fake `ExecutionEnv` registry: near-miss unique/ambiguous/exact, GC'd-with-log, malformed id (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5).
- `E2E-*` real-host PTY suites — the repo's existing seam for background jobs is the integration PTY family that drives R…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1447
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1447
- **Title**: gh-1438 bash_job: resolve near-miss/stale job ids instead of 'unknown background job' dead-ends bound status output GC exited jobs
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1438` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +1487
- **Deletions**: -39
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T11:53:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T13:01:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #1438
### What changed

`bash_job` no longer dead-ends on stale or near-miss job ids: an unknown id resolves to its closest retained job (read actions only), the no-id `status` listing is bounded, and the registry GCs exited entries (gh-1438).

### Key decisions

- **Pure resolution core** — new `lib/src/tools/job_id_resolution.dart`: id-shape parse (`sh-<n>-<tail>`), prefix match, edit-distance closeness, `matchShellJobId` (unique / ambiguous / closest-≤3). The registry maps matches onto entries (`ShellJobLookup` sealed types); the tool layer renders messages.
- **Resolution is read-only** — `output`/`status` act on a unique `sh-<n>-` near-miss (tail + corrected id + "stop polling the stale id"); `stop` never kills a guessed id, it only hints the closest ids (AC5). Malformed ids (`sh-99`, no tail) skip resolution and keep today's shortest error (E3, REG-green).
- **Bounded status** — no-id `status` = running jobs + last 20 exited (newest settle first) + a counts line; `all: true` restores the full dump (AC3, property-tested over 0/100/10k exited jobs).
- **Exited-entry GC** — `ShellJobRegistry(maxRetainedExitedJobs: 100)`: oldest-settled pruned LRU, log files stay on disk, a tombstone map lets exact-id `output` fall back to the on-disk log (AC4); deleted log degrades to the clean error (E2).
- **Settle stamps** — `ShellJobEntry.settledAt` (first observation wins) drives GC order and the new "exited Nm ago" context on exact-id results.
- **Schema kept budget-neutral** — the over-window guard prices every schema character (`estimateRequestOverheadTokens`, chars/4) against the model window, and `agent_cli_headless_over_window_test` sits ~25 tokens under the edge: the expanded `bash_job` schema tipped request 1 over (4 requests instead of 2). Final wording is compressed to near merge-base parity; semantics live in the runtime messages.
- The `jobs:` yaml knob was deliberately not added (its `0 = disabled` convention clashes with the registry's `0 = prune-all`); hosts configure via the constructor.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/tools/job_id_resolution_test.dart test/tools/shell_jobs_test.dart test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart
dart test test/cli/agent_cli_headless_over_window_test.dart   # schema-overhead budget guard
dart test --exclude-tags integration                           # full gate, 9.8k tests
```

<details><summary>Resolution flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[bash_job output/status id] --> LK{registry.lookup}
  LK -->|exact| HIT[tail + exited-Nm-ago context]
  LK|unique sh-n- prefix| NM[tail + corrected id + stop-polling note]
  LK|2+ share prefix| AMB[list candidates, no pick E1]
  LK|none| UNK{shape + GC tombstone}
  UNK|malformed| ERR[shortest error E3]
  UNK|pruned| DISK[tail from on-disk log AC4 / clean error E2]
  UNK|never registered| HINT[≤3 closest ids + do-not-retry AC2]
  REQ --> STOP[stop] -->|never resolves| HINT2[closest-ids hint only AC5]
```

</details>

# gh-1438: [WIP][GOAL] bash_job id-churn hardening — near-miss resolution, bounded status, exited-job GC

## Description

## Goal — bash_job id-churn hardening (v2, repair edit: mechanism + amplification + retracted framings + threat model + E2E layer; line numbers re-pinned)

One sentence: **`bash_job` becomes forgiving of stale and near-miss job ids** — an unknown id resolves to its closest retained job instead of dead-ending, and the tool's outputs stay bounded.

Observed in production (chief session, ~13h of monitor shifts): the agent re-polled job ids reconstructed from memory (correct `sh-NNNN-` numeric part, wrong hash suffix) — every poll returned a bare `unknown background job` error with zero recovery information, so the poll-per-turn loop survived for hundreds of turns. Separately, `bash_job status` with no id dumped 1600+ lines of exited jobs into the agent context.

## Why this framing

- ~~"Agent discipline problem — fix via prompt."~~ **RETRACTED.** The harness must be robust to imperfect id recall; a prompt-side "don't poll stale ids" fix depends on exactly the faculty that failed (memory reconstruction across hundreds of turns).
- ~~"Registry reaps finished jobs while notices still reference them."~~ **RETRACTED by evidence:** `_jobs` is grow-only — all ~1600 exited jobs were retained with their logs; the polled ids were **near-misses** (correct `sh-NNNN-` numeric part, wrong hash suffix), never reaped ids.
- ~~"Deduplicate settle notices."~~ **RETRACTED:** the notice path already carries suppression (`suppressSettleNotification`, lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:119; call site builtin_tools_bash.dart:490 — #562 shipped it). The loop was **poll-side**, not notice-side.

### Mechanism (falsifiable, step-1 form)

Settle wake arrives with the job id as free text → the agent answers `bash_job(output)` with an id reconstructed from memory → `job(id)` is an exact-match lookup over retained entries (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:215), so a one-char-wrong id is **indistinguishable from one that never existed** → the verb dead-ends in `StateError('unknown background job: $id')` (builtin_tools_bash.dart:586 / :606, shell_jobs.dart:300) with **zero recovery signal** — no near-miss candidates, no "exited Nm ago", no log-dir hint → each settle wake re-arms the same wrong poll.

### Why it survived ~13h / hundreds of turns (amplification)

The dead-end error is terminal and information-free: nothing in the result tells the agent to stop, re-derive, or look in `.fah/bash_jobs/`, so nothing breaks the loop from the tool side. Every iteration is answered with a competent one-line "routine" reply, which masks the loop in the transcript as normal task discharge — hours of successful-looking execution outweigh any lost instruction (self-precedent). And the agent's periodic no-id `bash_job status` flooded context with 1600+ exited-job status lines (observed live), burying the correct id under noise and further degrading id fidelity on the next reconstruction.

## Pinned facts (current code — verified against the working tree, this edit)

- `ShellJobRegistry._jobs` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:199) is a grow-only list — exited jobs are retained for the process lifetime with their logs; there is no GC and no cap. (pos: AC3 bounding holds over 0/100/10k retained; neg: current unbounded dump is the REG baseline)
- Exact-match lookup `ShellJobEntry? job(String id)` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:215) returns null on any mismatch. (pos: AC1 near-miss resolution; neg: E3 non-`sh-NNNN-` shape skips resolution)
- Unknown ids throw `StateError('unknown background job: $id')` from three verb paths: builtin_tools_bash.dart:586 (`status`), :606 (`stop`), shell_jobs.dart:300 (`tail`, used by `output`). (pos: AC2 non-error recovery result; neg: E2 clean error after GC+log deletion)
- `tail()` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:297) reads the job's log file raw. (pos: AC1 resolved tail; neg: E2 deleted-log degradation)
- `_bashJobStatusResult` (builtin_tools_bash.dart:576) with no id maps every retained entry 1:1 via `jobs.jobs.map(_shellJobStatusLine).join('\n')` — unbounded by construction. (pos: AC3 bounded rendering; neg: `all: true` opt-out still restores the full dump)
- Logs persist under `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log` and remain readable after exit; on-disk content is NOT redacted (see threat model).
- Retraction evidence: notice suppression exists — `suppressSettleNotification` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:119, called at builtin_tools_bash.dart:490).

## Capability surface (bash_job call shapes → behavior)

| call | today | becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `output`/`status` exact id, live or exited | works (tail from log) | unchanged, plus "exited Nm ago" context |
| `output` unknown id, unique `sh-NNNN-` prefix match among retained jobs | error dead-end | resolve: return that job's tail + corrected id + "already exited — stop polling the stale id" |
| `output`/`status` unknown id, ambiguous or no match | bare error | plain result listing up to 3 closest retained ids + "this id was never registered; do not retry" |
| `stop` unknown id | error dead-end | same closest-ids hint, but **never resolves**: destructive actions require the exact id |
| `status` no id | full dump (unbounded) | running jobs in full + last 20 exited + counts; `all: true` restores the full dump |
| registry growth | unbounded | **second tier**: cap retained exited entries (config, LRU by settle time; logs stay on disk); post-GC exact-id `output` falls back to the on-disk log |

**Invariant: resolution is read-only.** `output`/`status` may act on a resolved near-miss; `stop` never kills a guessed id.

**Tiering:** rows 1–5 are **core** (this card); registry GC is **second tier** (opt-in config, follow-up friendly); the excluded list below is **excluded** with rationale.

### Security threat model

- **Attacker-controlled inputs:** job **command strings** and **log content**. Logs are written to `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log` and read back **raw** by `tail()` — on-disk bytes are NOT redacted — and both flow into `status` lines and `output` tails. Resolution therefore must not surface MORE attacker-controlled text than today's exact-id path: same tail budget, same `_shellJobStatusLine` shape. Resolution changes routing, not volume.
- **Id-enumeration side-channel:** the ≤3 closest-ids candidate list is a minor enumeration aid. Job ids are session-local and not secrets — accepted risk, stated here rather than hidden; no rate-limiting.
- **Instruction hierarchy / destructive gate:** a typo'd or prompt-injected `bash_job stop` must never kill a job the caller did not name exactly. `stop` never acts on a resolved id (AC5) — only the exact id authorizes a destructive verb; resolution is hygiene, the exact-id requirement is the boundary.
- **Impossible by construction:** resolution never fabricates log content — it returns `tail()` of a retained entry's real file, or the same clean error as today (E2).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — `output` with a near-miss id (same `sh-NNNN-` prefix, wrong suffix, exactly one retained match) returns the resolved job's tail, names the corrected id, and states it already exited. (IT, fake registry/env; E2E-1)
- **AC2** — unresolvable unknown id returns a NON-error result with ≤3 closest ids and an explicit do-not-retry note. (IT)
- **AC3** — `status` no-id output line count = running + min(exited, 20) + summary, verified as a property over registries with 0/100/10k exited jobs. (UT/IT; E2E-2)
- **AC4** — after GC prunes an exited entry, exact-id `output` still returns the tail from the on-disk log while the log exists; deleted log degrades to today's clean error. (IT)
- **AC5** — `stop` never acts on a resolved near-miss id (asserted: no kill call, hint returned). (IT)

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, layered UT/IT/E2E/REG

- `UT-*` pure id-distance/prefix resolution + status-bounding math (AC1/AC3).
- `IT-*` fake `ExecutionEnv` registry: near-miss unique/ambiguous/exact, GC'd-with-log, malformed id (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5).
- `E2E-*` real-host PTY suites — the repo's existing seam for background jobs is the integration PTY family that drives R…

- `UT-*` pure id-distance/prefix resolution + status-bounding math (AC1/AC3).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1447
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1447
- **Title**: gh-1438 bash_job: resolve near-miss/stale job ids instead of 'unknown background job' dead-ends bound status output GC exited jobs
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1438` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +1487
- **Deletions**: -39
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T11:53:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T13:01:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #1438
### What changed

`bash_job` no longer dead-ends on stale or near-miss job ids: an unknown id resolves to its closest retained job (read actions only), the no-id `status` listing is bounded, and the registry GCs exited entries (gh-1438).

### Key decisions

- **Pure resolution core** — new `lib/src/tools/job_id_resolution.dart`: id-shape parse (`sh-<n>-<tail>`), prefix match, edit-distance closeness, `matchShellJobId` (unique / ambiguous / closest-≤3). The registry maps matches onto entries (`ShellJobLookup` sealed types); the tool layer renders messages.
- **Resolution is read-only** — `output`/`status` act on a unique `sh-<n>-` near-miss (tail + corrected id + "stop polling the stale id"); `stop` never kills a guessed id, it only hints the closest ids (AC5). Malformed ids (`sh-99`, no tail) skip resolution and keep today's shortest error (E3, REG-green).
- **Bounded status** — no-id `status` = running jobs + last 20 exited (newest settle first) + a counts line; `all: true` restores the full dump (AC3, property-tested over 0/100/10k exited jobs).
- **Exited-entry GC** — `ShellJobRegistry(maxRetainedExitedJobs: 100)`: oldest-settled pruned LRU, log files stay on disk, a tombstone map lets exact-id `output` fall back to the on-disk log (AC4); deleted log degrades to the clean error (E2).
- **Settle stamps** — `ShellJobEntry.settledAt` (first observation wins) drives GC order and the new "exited Nm ago" context on exact-id results.
- **Schema kept budget-neutral** — the over-window guard prices every schema character (`estimateRequestOverheadTokens`, chars/4) against the model window, and `agent_cli_headless_over_window_test` sits ~25 tokens under the edge: the expanded `bash_job` schema tipped request 1 over (4 requests instead of 2). Final wording is compressed to near merge-base parity; semantics live in the runtime messages.
- The `jobs:` yaml knob was deliberately not added (its `0 = disabled` convention clashes with the registry's `0 = prune-all`); hosts configure via the constructor.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/tools/job_id_resolution_test.dart test/tools/shell_jobs_test.dart test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart
dart test test/cli/agent_cli_headless_over_window_test.dart   # schema-overhead budget guard
dart test --exclude-tags integration                           # full gate, 9.8k tests
```

<details><summary>Resolution flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[bash_job output/status id] --> LK{registry.lookup}
  LK -->|exact| HIT[tail + exited-Nm-ago context]
  LK|unique sh-n- prefix| NM[tail + corrected id + stop-polling note]
  LK|2+ share prefix| AMB[list candidates, no pick E1]
  LK|none| UNK{shape + GC tombstone}
  UNK|malformed| ERR[shortest error E3]
  UNK|pruned| DISK[tail from on-disk log AC4 / clean error E2]
  UNK|never registered| HINT[≤3 closest ids + do-not-retry AC2]

# gh-1438: [WIP][GOAL] bash_job id-churn hardening — near-miss resolution, bounded status, exited-job GC

## Description

## Goal — bash_job id-churn hardening (v2, repair edit: mechanism + amplification + retracted framings + threat model + E2E layer; line numbers re-pinned)

One sentence: **`bash_job` becomes forgiving of stale and near-miss job ids** — an unknown id resolves to its closest retained job instead of dead-ending, and the tool's outputs stay bounded.

Observed in production (chief session, ~13h of monitor shifts): the agent re-polled job ids reconstructed from memory (correct `sh-NNNN-` numeric part, wrong hash suffix) — every poll returned a bare `unknown background job` error with zero recovery information, so the poll-per-turn loop survived for hundreds of turns. Separately, `bash_job status` with no id dumped 1600+ lines of exited jobs into the agent context.

## Why this framing

- ~~"Agent discipline problem — fix via prompt."~~ **RETRACTED.** The harness must be robust to imperfect id recall; a prompt-side "don't poll stale ids" fix depends on exactly the faculty that failed (memory reconstruction across hundreds of turns).
- ~~"Registry reaps finished jobs while notices still reference them."~~ **RETRACTED by evidence:** `_jobs` is grow-only — all ~1600 exited jobs were retained with their logs; the polled ids were **near-misses** (correct `sh-NNNN-` numeric part, wrong hash suffix), never reaped ids.
- ~~"Deduplicate settle notices."~~ **RETRACTED:** the notice path already carries suppression (`suppressSettleNotification`, lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:119; call site builtin_tools_bash.dart:490 — #562 shipped it). The loop was **poll-side**, not notice-side.

### Mechanism (falsifiable, step-1 form)

Settle wake arrives with the job id as free text → the agent answers `bash_job(output)` with an id reconstructed from memory → `job(id)` is an exact-match lookup over retained entries (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:215), so a one-char-wrong id is **indistinguishable from one that never existed** → the verb dead-ends in `StateError('unknown background job: $id')` (builtin_tools_bash.dart:586 / :606, shell_jobs.dart:300) with **zero recovery signal** — no near-miss candidates, no "exited Nm ago", no log-dir hint → each settle wake re-arms the same wrong poll.

### Why it survived ~13h / hundreds of turns (amplification)

The dead-end error is terminal and information-free: nothing in the result tells the agent to stop, re-derive, or look in `.fah/bash_jobs/`, so nothing breaks the loop from the tool side. Every iteration is answered with a competent one-line "routine" reply, which masks the loop in the transcript as normal task discharge — hours of successful-looking execution outweigh any lost instruction (self-precedent). And the agent's periodic no-id `bash_job status` flooded context with 1600+ exited-job status lines (observed live), burying the correct id under noise and further degrading id fidelity on the next reconstruction.

## Pinned facts (current code — verified against the working tree, this edit)

- `ShellJobRegistry._jobs` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:199) is a grow-only list — exited jobs are retained for the process lifetime with their logs; there is no GC and no cap. (pos: AC3 bounding holds over 0/100/10k retained; neg: current unbounded dump is the REG baseline)
- Exact-match lookup `ShellJobEntry? job(String id)` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:215) returns null on any mismatch. (pos: AC1 near-miss resolution; neg: E3 non-`sh-NNNN-` shape skips resolution)
- Unknown ids throw `StateError('unknown background job: $id')` from three verb paths: builtin_tools_bash.dart:586 (`status`), :606 (`stop`), shell_jobs.dart:300 (`tail`, used by `output`). (pos: AC2 non-error recovery result; neg: E2 clean error after GC+log deletion)
- `tail()` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:297) reads the job's log file raw. (pos: AC1 resolved tail; neg: E2 deleted-log degradation)
- `_bashJobStatusResult` (builtin_tools_bash.dart:576) with no id maps every retained entry 1:1 via `jobs.jobs.map(_shellJobStatusLine).join('\n')` — unbounded by construction. (pos: AC3 bounded rendering; neg: `all: true` opt-out still restores the full dump)
- Logs persist under `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log` and remain readable after exit; on-disk content is NOT redacted (see threat model).
- Retraction evidence: notice suppression exists — `suppressSettleNotification` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:119, called at builtin_tools_bash.dart:490).

## Capability surface (bash_job call shapes → behavior)

| call | today | becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `output`/`status` exact id, live or exited | works (tail from log) | unchanged, plus "exited Nm ago" context |
| `output` unknown id, unique `sh-NNNN-` prefix match among retained jobs | error dead-end | resolve: return that job's tail + corrected id + "already exited — stop polling the stale id" |
| `output`/`status` unknown id, ambiguous or no match | bare error | plain result listing up to 3 closest retained ids + "this id was never registered; do not retry" |
| `stop` unknown id | error dead-end | same closest-ids hint, but **never resolves**: destructive actions require the exact id |
| `status` no id | full dump (unbounded) | running jobs in full + last 20 exited + counts; `all: true` restores the full dump |
| registry growth | unbounded | **second tier**: cap retained exited entries (config, LRU by settle time; logs stay on disk); post-GC exact-id `output` falls back to the on-disk log |

**Invariant: resolution is read-only.** `output`/`status` may act on a resolved near-miss; `stop` never kills a guessed id.

**Tiering:** rows 1–5 are **core** (this card); registry GC is **second tier** (opt-in config, follow-up friendly); the excluded list below is **excluded** with rationale.

### Security threat model

- **Attacker-controlled inputs:** job **command strings** and **log content**. Logs are written to `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log` and read back **raw** by `tail()` — on-disk bytes are NOT redacted — and both flow into `status` lines and `output` tails. Resolution therefore must not surface MORE attacker-controlled text than today's exact-id path: same tail budget, same `_shellJobStatusLine` shape. Resolution changes routing, not volume.
- **Id-enumeration side-channel:** the ≤3 closest-ids candidate list is a minor enumeration aid. Job ids are session-local and not secrets — accepted risk, stated here rather than hidden; no rate-limiting.
- **Instruction hierarchy / destructive gate:** a typo'd or prompt-injected `bash_job stop` must never kill a job the caller did not name exactly. `stop` never acts on a resolved id (AC5) — only the exact id authorizes a destructive verb; resolution is hygiene, the exact-id requirement is the boundary.
- **Impossible by construction:** resolution never fabricates log content — it returns `tail()` of a retained entry's real file, or the same clean error as today (E2).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — `output` with a near-miss id (same `sh-NNNN-` prefix, wrong suffix, exactly one retained match) returns the resolved job's tail, names the corrected id, and states it already exited. (IT, fake registry/env; E2E-1)

One sentence: **`bash_job` becomes forgiving of stale and near-miss job ids** — an unknown id resolves to its closest retained job instead of dead-ending, and the tool's outputs stay bounded.

Observed in production (chief session, ~13h of monitor shifts): the agent re-polled job ids reconstructed from memory (correct `sh-NNNN-` numeric part, wrong hash suffix) — every poll returned a bare `unknown background job` error with zero recovery information, so the poll-per-turn loop survived for hundreds of turns. ## Why this framing

- ~~"Agent discipline problem — fix via prompt."~~ **RETRACTED.** The harness must be robust to imperfect id recall; a prompt-side "don't poll stale ids" fix depends on exactly the faculty that failed (memory reconstruction across hundreds of turns).

- ~~"Deduplicate settle notices."~~ **RETRACTED:** the notice path already carries suppression (`suppressSettleNotification`, lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:119; call site builtin_tools_bash.dart:490 — #562 shipped it). The loop was **poll-side**, not notice-side.

### Mechanism (falsifiable, step-1 form)

Settle wake arrives with the job id as free text → the agent answers `bash_job(output)` with an id reconstructed from memory → `job(id)` is an exact-match lookup over retained entries (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:215), so a one-char-wrong id is **indistinguishable from one that never existed** → the verb dead-ends in `StateError('unknown background job: $id')` (builtin_tools_bash.dart:586 / :606, shell_jobs.dart:300) with **zero recovery signal** — no near-miss candidates, no "exited Nm ago", no log-dir hint → each settle wake re-arms the same wrong poll.

### Why it survived ~13h / hundreds of turns (amplification)

The dead-end error is terminal and information-free: nothing in the result tells the agent to stop, re-derive, or look in `.fah/bash_jobs/`, so nothing breaks the loop from the tool side. Every iteration is answered with a competent one-line "routine" reply, which masks the loop in the transcript as normal task discharge — hours of successful-looking execution outweigh any lost instruction (self-precedent). - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1447
- **Title**: gh-1438 bash_job: resolve near-miss/stale job ids instead of 'unknown background job' dead-ends bound status output GC exited jobs
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1438` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +1487
- **Deletions**: -39
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T11:53:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T13:01:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #1438
### What changed

`bash_job` no longer dead-ends on stale or near-miss job ids: an unknown id resolves to its closest retained job (read actions only), the no-id `status` listing is bounded, and the registry GCs exited entries (gh-1438).

### Key decisions

- **Pure resolution core** — new `lib/src/tools/job_id_resolution.dart`: id-shape parse (`sh-<n>-<tail>`), prefix match, edit-distance closeness, `matchShellJobId` (unique / ambiguous / closest-≤3). The registry maps matches onto entries (`ShellJobLookup` sealed types); the tool layer renders messages.
- **Resolution is read-only** — `output`/`status` act on a unique `sh-<n>-` near-miss (tail + corrected id + "stop polling the stale id"); `stop` never kills a guessed id, it only hints the closest ids (AC5). Malformed ids (`sh-99`, no tail) skip resolution and keep today's shortest error (E3, REG-green).
- **Bounded status** — no-id `status` = running jobs + last 20 exited (newest settle first) + a counts line; `all: true` restores the full dump (AC3, property-tested over 0/100/10k exited jobs).
- **Exited-entry GC** — `ShellJobRegistry(maxRetainedExitedJobs: 100)`: oldest-settled pruned LRU, log files stay on disk, a tombstone map lets exact-id `output` fall back to the on-disk log (AC4); deleted log degrades to the clean error (E2).
- **Settle stamps** — `ShellJobEntry.settledAt` (first observation wins) drives GC order and the new "exited Nm ago" context on exact-id results.
- **Schema kept budget-neutral** — the over-window guard prices every schema character (`estimateRequestOverheadTokens`, chars/4) against the model window, and `agent_cli_headless_over_window_test` sits ~25 tokens under the edge: the expanded `bash_job` schema tipped request 1 over (4 requests instead of 2). Final wording is compressed to near merge-base parity; semantics live in the runtime messages.
- The `jobs:` yaml knob was deliberately not added (its `0 = disabled` convention clashes with the registry's `0 = prune-all`); hosts configure via the constructor.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/tools/job_id_resolution_test.dart test/tools/shell_jobs_test.dart test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart
dart test test/cli/agent_cli_headless_over_window_test.dart   # schema-overhead budget guard
dart test --exclude-tags integration                           # full gate, 9.8k tests
```

flowchart TD

  LK -->|exact| HIT[tail + exited-Nm-ago context]
  LK|unique sh-n- prefix| NM[tail + corrected id + stop-polling note]

  LK|none| UNK{shape + GC tombstone}

# gh-1438: [WIP][GOAL] bash_job id-churn hardening — near-miss resolution, bounded status, exited-job GC

## Description

## Goal — bash_job id-churn hardening (v2, repair edit: mechanism + amplification + retracted framings + threat model + E2E layer; line numbers re-pinned)

One sentence: **`bash_job` becomes forgiving of stale and near-miss job ids** — an unknown id resolves to its closest retained job instead of dead-ending, and the tool's outputs stay bounded.

Observed in production (chief session, ~13h of monitor shifts): the agent re-polled job ids reconstructed from memory (correct `sh-NNNN-` numeric part, wrong hash suffix) — every poll returned a bare `unknown background job` error with zero recovery information, so the poll-per-turn loop survived for hundreds of turns. Separately, `bash_job status` with no id dumped 1600+ lines of exited jobs into the agent context.

## Why this framing

- ~~"Agent discipline problem — fix via prompt."~~ **RETRACTED.** The harness must be robust to imperfect id recall; a prompt-side "don't poll stale ids" fix depends on exactly the faculty that failed (memory reconstruction across hundreds of turns).
- ~~"Registry reaps finished jobs while notices still reference them."~~ **RETRACTED by evidence:** `_jobs` is grow-only — all ~1600 exited jobs were retained with their logs; the polled ids were **near-misses** (correct `sh-NNNN-` numeric part, wrong hash suffix), never reaped ids.
- ~~"Deduplicate settle notices."~~ **RETRACTED:** the notice path already carries suppression (`suppressSettleNotification`, lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:119; call site builtin_tools_bash.dart:490 — #562 shipped it). The loop was **poll-side**, not notice-side.

### Mechanism (falsifiable, step-1 form)

Settle wake arrives with the job id as free text → the agent answers `bash_job(output)` with an id reconstructed from memory → `job(id)` is an exact-match lookup over retained entries (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:215), so a one-char-wrong id is **indistinguishable from one that never existed** → the verb dead-ends in `StateError('unknown background job: $id')` (builtin_tools_bash.dart:586 / :606, shell_jobs.dart:300) with **zero recovery signal** — no near-miss candidates, no "exited Nm ago", no log-dir hint → each settle wake re-arms the same wrong poll.

### Why it survived ~13h / hundreds of turns (amplification)

The dead-end error is terminal and information-free: nothing in the result tells the agent to stop, re-derive, or look in `.fah/bash_jobs/`, so nothing breaks the loop from the tool side. Every iteration is answered with a competent one-line "routine" reply, which masks the loop in the transcript as normal task discharge — hours of successful-looking execution outweigh any lost instruction (self-precedent). And the agent's periodic no-id `bash_job status` flooded context with 1600+ exited-job status lines (observed live), burying the correct id under noise and further degrading id fidelity on the next reconstruction.

## Pinned facts (current code — verified against the working tree, this edit)

- `ShellJobRegistry._jobs` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:199) is a grow-only list — exited jobs are retained for the process lifetime with their logs; there is no GC and no cap. (pos: AC3 bounding holds over 0/100/10k retained; neg: current unbounded dump is the REG baseline)
- Exact-match lookup `ShellJobEntry? job(String id)` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:215) returns null on any mismatch. (pos: AC1 near-miss resolution; neg: E3 non-`sh-NNNN-` shape skips resolution)
- Unknown ids throw `StateError('unknown background job: $id')` from three verb paths: builtin_tools_bash.dart:586 (`status`), :606 (`stop`), shell_jobs.dart:300 (`tail`, used by `output`). (pos: AC2 non-error recovery result; neg: E2 clean error after GC+log deletion)
- `tail()` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:297) reads the job's log file raw. (pos: AC1 resolved tail; neg: E2 deleted-log degradation)
- `_bashJobStatusResult` (builtin_tools_bash.dart:576) with no id maps every retained entry 1:1 via `jobs.jobs.map(_shellJobStatusLine).join('\n')` — unbounded by construction. (pos: AC3 bounded rendering; neg: `all: true` opt-out still restores the full dump)
- Logs persist under `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log` and remain readable after exit; on-disk content is NOT redacted (see threat model).
- Retraction evidence: notice suppression exists — `suppressSettleNotification` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:119, called at builtin_tools_bash.dart:490).

## Capability surface (bash_job call shapes → behavior)

| call | today | becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `output`/`status` exact id, live or exited | works (tail from log) | unchanged, plus "exited Nm ago" context |
| `output` unknown id, unique `sh-NNNN-` prefix match among retained jobs | error dead-end | resolve: return that job's tail + corrected id + "already exited — stop polling the stale id" |
| `output`/`status` unknown id, ambiguous or no match | bare error | plain result listing up to 3 closest retained ids + "this id was never registered; do not retry" |
| `stop` unknown id | error dead-end | same closest-ids hint, but **never resolves**: destructive actions require the exact id |
| `status` no id | full dump (unbounded) | running jobs in full + last 20 exited + counts; `all: true` restores the full dump |
| registry growth | unbounded | **second tier**: cap retained exited entries (config, LRU by settle time; logs stay on disk); post-GC exact-id `output` falls back to the on-disk log |

**Invariant: resolution is read-only.** `output`/`status` may act on a resolved near-miss; `stop` never kills a guessed id.

**Tiering:** rows 1–5 are **core** (this card); registry GC is **second tier** (opt-in config, follow-up friendly); the excluded list below is **excluded** with rationale.

### Security threat model

- **Attacker-controlled inputs:** job **command strings** and **log content**. Logs are written to `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log` and read back **raw** by `tail()` — on-disk bytes are NOT redacted — and both flow into `status` lines and `output` tails. Resolution therefore must not surface MORE attacker-controlled text than today's exact-id path: same tail budget, same `_shellJobStatusLine` shape. Resolution changes routing, not volume.
- **Id-enumeration side-channel:** the ≤3 closest-ids candidate list is a minor enumeration aid. Job ids are session-local and not secrets — accepted risk, stated here rather than hidden; no rate-limiting.
- **Instruction hierarchy / destructive gate:** a typo'd or prompt-injected `bash_job stop` must never kill a job the caller did not name exactly. `stop` never acts on a resolved id (AC5) — only the exact id authorizes a destructive verb; resolution is hygiene, the exact-id requirement is the boundary.
- **Impossible by construction:** resolution never fabricates log content — it returns `tail()` of a retained entry's real file, or the same clean error as today (E2).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — `output` with a near-miss id (same `sh-NNNN-` prefix, wrong suffix, exactly one retained match) returns the resolved job's tail, names the corrected id, and states it already exited. (IT, fake registry/env; E2E-1)
- **AC2** — unresolvable unknown id returns a NON-error result with ≤3 closest ids and an explicit do-not-retry note. (IT)
- **AC3** — `status` no-id output line count = running + min(exited, 20) + summary, verified as a property over registries with 0/100/10k exited jobs. (UT/IT; E2E-2)
- **AC4** — after GC prunes an exited entry, exact-id `output` still returns the tail from the on-disk log while the log exists; deleted log degrades to today's clean error. (IT)
- **AC5** — `stop` never acts on a resolved near-miss id (asserted: no kill call, hint returned). (IT)

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, layered UT/IT/E2E/REG

- `UT-*` pure id-distance/prefix resolution + status-bounding math (AC1/AC3).
- `IT-*` fake `ExecutionEnv` registry: near-miss unique/ambiguous/exact, GC'd-with-log, malformed id (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5).
- `E2E-*` real-host PTY suites — the repo's existing seam for background jobs is the integration PTY family that drives R…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1447
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1447
- **Title**: gh-1438 bash_job: resolve near-miss/stale job ids instead of 'unknown background job' dead-ends bound status output GC exited jobs
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1438` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +1487
- **Deletions**: -39
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T11:53:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T13:01:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #1438
### What changed

`bash_job` no longer dead-ends on stale or near-miss job ids: an unknown id resolves to its closest retained job (read actions only), the no-id `status` listing is bounded, and the registry GCs exited entries (gh-1438).

### Key decisions

- **Pure resolution core** — new `lib/src/tools/job_id_resolution.dart`: id-shape parse (`sh-<n>-<tail>`), prefix match, edit-distance closeness, `matchShellJobId` (unique / ambiguous / closest-≤3). The registry maps matches onto entries (`ShellJobLookup` sealed types); the tool layer renders messages.
- **Resolution is read-only** — `output`/`status` act on a unique `sh-<n>-` near-miss (tail + corrected id + "stop polling the stale id"); `stop` never kills a guessed id, it only hints the closest ids (AC5). Malformed ids (`sh-99`, no tail) skip resolution and keep today's shortest error (E3, REG-green).
- **Bounded status** — no-id `status` = running jobs + last 20 exited (newest settle first) + a counts line; `all: true` restores the full dump (AC3, property-tested over 0/100/10k exited jobs).
- **Exited-entry GC** — `ShellJobRegistry(maxRetainedExitedJobs: 100)`: oldest-settled pruned LRU, log files stay on disk, a tombstone map lets exact-id `output` fall back to the on-disk log (AC4); deleted log degrades to the clean error (E2).
- **Settle stamps** — `ShellJobEntry.settledAt` (first observation wins) drives GC order and the new "exited Nm ago" context on exact-id results.
- **Schema kept budget-neutral** — the over-window guard prices every schema character (`estimateRequestOverheadTokens`, chars/4) against the model window, and `agent_cli_headless_over_window_test` sits ~25 tokens under the edge: the expanded `bash_job` schema tipped request 1 over (4 requests instead of 2). Final wording is compressed to near merge-base parity; semantics live in the runtime messages.
- The `jobs:` yaml knob was deliberately not added (its `0 = disabled` convention clashes with the registry's `0 = prune-all`); hosts configure via the constructor.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/tools/job_id_resolution_test.dart test/tools/shell_jobs_test.dart test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart
dart test test/cli/agent_cli_headless_over_window_test.dart   # schema-overhead budget guard
dart test --exclude-tags integration                           # full gate, 9.8k tests
```

<details><summary>Resolution flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[bash_job output/status id] --> LK{registry.lookup}
  LK -->|exact| HIT[tail + exited-Nm-ago context]
  LK|unique sh-n- prefix| NM[tail + corrected id + stop-polling note]
  LK|2+ share prefix| AMB[list candidates, no pick E1]
  LK|none| UNK{shape + GC tombstone}
  UNK|malformed| ERR[shortest error E3]
  UNK|pruned| DISK[tail from on-disk log AC4 / clean error E2]
  UNK|never registered| HINT[≤3 closest ids + do-not-retry AC2]
  REQ --> STOP[stop] -->|never resolves| HINT2[closest-ids hint only AC5]
```

# gh-1438: [WIP][GOAL] bash_job id-churn hardening — near-miss resolution, bounded status, exited-job GC

## Description

## Goal — bash_job id-churn hardening (v2, repair edit: mechanism + amplification + retracted framings + threat model + E2E layer; line numbers re-pinned)

One sentence: **`bash_job` becomes forgiving of stale and near-miss job ids** — an unknown id resolves to its closest retained job instead of dead-ending, and the tool's outputs stay bounded.

Observed in production (chief session, ~13h of monitor shifts): the agent re-polled job ids reconstructed from memory (correct `sh-NNNN-` numeric part, wrong hash suffix) — every poll returned a bare `unknown background job` error with zero recovery information, so the poll-per-turn loop survived for hundreds of turns. Separately, `bash_job status` with no id dumped 1600+ lines of exited jobs into the agent context.

## Why this framing

- ~~"Agent discipline problem — fix via prompt."~~ **RETRACTED.** The harness must be robust to imperfect id recall; a prompt-side "don't poll stale ids" fix depends on exactly the faculty that failed (memory reconstruction across hundreds of turns).
- ~~"Registry reaps finished jobs while notices still reference them."~~ **RETRACTED by evidence:** `_jobs` is grow-only — all ~1600 exited jobs were retained with their logs; the polled ids were **near-misses** (correct `sh-NNNN-` numeric part, wrong hash suffix), never reaped ids.
- ~~"Deduplicate settle notices."~~ **RETRACTED:** the notice path already carries suppression (`suppressSettleNotification`, lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:119; call site builtin_tools_bash.dart:490 — #562 shipped it). The loop was **poll-side**, not notice-side.

### Mechanism (falsifiable, step-1 form)

Settle wake arrives with the job id as free text → the agent answers `bash_job(output)` with an id reconstructed from memory → `job(id)` is an exact-match lookup over retained entries (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:215), so a one-char-wrong id is **indistinguishable from one that never existed** → the verb dead-ends in `StateError('unknown background job: $id')` (builtin_tools_bash.dart:586 / :606, shell_jobs.dart:300) with **zero recovery signal** — no near-miss candidates, no "exited Nm ago", no log-dir hint → each settle wake re-arms the same wrong poll.

### Why it survived ~13h / hundreds of turns (amplification)

The dead-end error is terminal and information-free: nothing in the result tells the agent to stop, re-derive, or look in `.fah/bash_jobs/`, so nothing breaks the loop from the tool side. Every iteration is answered with a competent one-line "routine" reply, which masks the loop in the transcript as normal task discharge — hours of successful-looking execution outweigh any lost instruction (self-precedent). And the agent's periodic no-id `bash_job status` flooded context with 1600+ exited-job status lines (observed live), burying the correct id under noise and further degrading id fidelity on the next reconstruction.

## Pinned facts (current code — verified against the working tree, this edit)

- `ShellJobRegistry._jobs` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:199) is a grow-only list — exited jobs are retained for the process lifetime with their logs; there is no GC and no cap. (pos: AC3 bounding holds over 0/100/10k retained; neg: current unbounded dump is the REG baseline)
- Exact-match lookup `ShellJobEntry? job(String id)` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:215) returns null on any mismatch. (pos: AC1 near-miss resolution; neg: E3 non-`sh-NNNN-` shape skips resolution)
- Unknown ids throw `StateError('unknown background job: $id')` from three verb paths: builtin_tools_bash.dart:586 (`status`), :606 (`stop`), shell_jobs.dart:300 (`tail`, used by `output`). (pos: AC2 non-error recovery result; neg: E2 clean error after GC+log deletion)
- `tail()` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:297) reads the job's log file raw. (pos: AC1 resolved tail; neg: E2 deleted-log degradation)
- `_bashJobStatusResult` (builtin_tools_bash.dart:576) with no id maps every retained entry 1:1 via `jobs.jobs.map(_shellJobStatusLine).join('\n')` — unbounded by construction. (pos: AC3 bounded rendering; neg: `all: true` opt-out still restores the full dump)
- Logs persist under `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log` and remain readable after exit; on-disk content is NOT redacted (see threat model).
- Retraction evidence: notice suppression exists — `suppressSettleNotification` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:119, called at builtin_tools_bash.dart:490).

## Capability surface (bash_job call shapes → behavior)

| call | today | becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `output`/`status` exact id, live or exited | works (tail from log) | unchanged, plus "exited Nm ago" context |
| `output` unknown id, unique `sh-NNNN-` prefix match among retained jobs | error dead-end | resolve: return that job's tail + corrected id + "already exited — stop polling the stale id" |
| `output`/`status` unknown id, ambiguous or no match | bare error | plain result listing up to 3 closest retained ids + "this id was never registered; do not retry" |
| `stop` unknown id | error dead-end | same closest-ids hint, but **never resolves**: destructive actions require the exact id |
| `status` no id | full dump (unbounded) | running jobs in full + last 20 exited + counts; `all: true` restores the full dump |
| registry growth | unbounded | **second tier**: cap retained exited entries (config, LRU by settle time; logs stay on disk); post-GC exact-id `output` falls back to the on-disk log |

**Invariant: resolution is read-only.** `output`/`status` may act on a resolved near-miss; `stop` never kills a guessed id.

**Tiering:** rows 1–5 are **core** (this card); registry GC is **second tier** (opt-in config, follow-up friendly); the excluded list below is **excluded** with rationale.

### Security threat model

- **Attacker-controlled inputs:** job **command strings** and **log content**. Logs are written to `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log` and read back **raw** by `tail()` — on-disk bytes are NOT redacted — and both flow into `status` lines and `output` tails. Resolution therefore must not surface MORE attacker-controlled text than today's exact-id path: same tail budget, same `_shellJobStatusLine` shape. Resolution changes routing, not volume.
- **Id-enumeration side-channel:** the ≤3 closest-ids candidate list is a minor enumeration aid. Job ids are session-local and not secrets — accepted risk, stated here rather than hidden; no rate-limiting.
- **Instruction hierarchy / destructive gate:** a typo'd or prompt-injected `bash_job stop` must never kill a job the caller did not name exactly. `stop` never acts on a resolved id (AC5) — only the exact id authorizes a destructive verb; resolution is hygiene, the exact-id requirement is the boundary.
- **Impossible by construction:** resolution never fabricates log content — it returns `tail()` of a retained entry's real file, or the same clean error as today (E2).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — `output` with a near-miss id (same `sh-NNNN-` prefix, wrong suffix, exactly one retained match) returns the resolved job's tail, names the corrected id, and states it already exited. (IT, fake registry/env; E2E-1)
- **AC2** — unresolvable unknown id returns a NON-error result with ≤3 closest ids and an explicit do-not-retry note. (IT)
- **AC3** — `status` no-id output line count = running + min(exited, 20) + summary, verified as a property over registries with 0/100/10k exited jobs. (UT/IT; E2E-2)
- **AC4** — after GC prunes an exited entry, exact-id `output` still returns the tail from the on-disk log while the log exists; deleted log degrades to today's clean error. (IT)
- **AC5** — `stop` never acts on a resolved near-miss id (asserted: no kill call, hint returned). (IT)

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, layered UT/IT/E2E/REG

- `UT-*` pure id-distance/prefix resolution + status-bounding math (AC1/AC3).
- `IT-*` fake `ExecutionEnv` registry: near-miss unique/ambiguous/exact, GC'd-with-log, malformed id (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5).
- `E2E-*` real-host PTY suites — the repo's existing seam for background jobs is the integration PTY family that drives R…

Observed in production (chief session, ~13h of monitor shifts): the agent re-polled job ids reconstructed from memory (correct `sh-NNNN-` numeric part, wrong hash suffix) — every poll returned a bare `unknown background job` error with zero recovery information, so the poll-per-turn loop survived for hundreds of turns. Separately, `bash_job status` with no id dumped 1600+ lines of exited jobs into the agent context.

## Why this framing

- ~~"Agent discipline problem — fix via prompt."~~ **RETRACTED.** The harness must be robust to imperfect id recall; a prompt-side "don't poll stale ids" fix depends on exactly the faculty that failed (memory reconstruction across hundreds of turns).
- ~~"Registry reaps finished jobs while notices still reference them."~~ **RETRACTED by evidence:** `_jobs` is grow-only — all ~1600 exited jobs were retained with their logs; the polled ids were **near-misses** (correct `sh-NNNN-` numeric part, wrong hash suffix), never reaped ids.
- ~~"Deduplicate settle notices."~~ **RETRACTED:** the notice path already carries suppression (`suppressSettleNotification`, lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:119; call site builtin_tools_bash.dart:490 — #562 shipped it). The loop was **poll-side**, not notice-side.

### Mechanism (falsifiable, step-1 form)

Settle wake arrives with the job id as free text → the agent answers `bash_job(output)` with an id reconstructed from memory → `job(id)` is an exact-match lookup over retained entries (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:215), so a one-char-wrong id is **indistinguishable from one that never existed** → the verb dead-ends in `StateError('unknown background job: $id')` (builtin_tools_bash.dart:586 / :606, shell_jobs.dart:300) with **zero recovery signal** — no near-miss candidates, no "exited Nm ago", no log-dir hint → each settle wake re-arms the same wrong poll.

### Why it survived ~13h / hundreds of turns (amplification)

The dead-end error is terminal and information-free: nothing in the result tells the agent to stop, re-derive, or look in `.fah/bash_jobs/`, so nothing breaks the loop from the tool side. Every iteration is answered with a competent one-line "routine" reply, which masks the loop in the transcript as normal task discharge — hours of successful-looking execution outweigh any lost instruction (self-precedent). And the agent's periodic no-id `bash_job status` flooded context with 1600+ exited-job status lines (observed live), burying the correct id under noise and further degrading id fidelity on the next reconstruction.

## Pinned facts (current code — verified against the working tree, this edit)

- `ShellJobRegistry._jobs` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:199) is a grow-only list — exited jobs are retained for the process lifetime with their logs; there is no GC and no cap. (pos: AC3 bounding holds over 0/100/10k retained; neg: current unbounded dump is the REG baseline)
- Exact-match lookup `ShellJobEntry? job(String id)` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:215) returns null on any mismatch. (pos: AC1 near-miss resolution; neg: E3 non-`sh-NNNN-` shape skips resolution)
- Unknown ids throw `StateError('unknown background job: $id')` from three verb paths: builtin_tools_bash.dart:586 (`status`), :606 (`stop`), shell_jobs.dart:300 (`tail`, used by `output`). (pos: AC2 non-error recovery result; neg: E2 clean error after GC+log deletion)
- `tail()` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:297) reads the job's log file raw. (pos: AC1 resolved tail; neg: E2 deleted-log degradation)
- `_bashJobStatusResult` (builtin_tools_bash.dart:576) with no id maps every retained entry 1:1 via `jobs.jobs.map(_shellJobStatusLine).join('\n')` — unbounded by construction. (pos: AC3 bounded rendering; neg: `all: true` opt-out still restores the full dump)
- Logs persist under `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log` and remain readable after exit; on-disk content is NOT redacted (see threat model).
- Retraction evidence: notice suppression exists — `suppressSettleNotification` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:119, called at builtin_tools_bash.dart:490).

## Capability surface (bash_job call shapes → behavior)

| call | today | becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `output`/`status` exact id, live or exited | works (tail from log) | unchanged, plus "exited Nm ago" context |
| `output` unknown id, unique `sh-NNNN-` prefix match among retained jobs | error dead-end | resolve: return that job's tail + corrected id + "already exited — stop polling the stale id" |
| `output`/`status` unknown id, ambiguous or no match | bare error | plain result listing up to 3 closest retained ids + "this id was never registered; do not retry" |
| `stop` unknown id | error dead-end | same closest-ids hint, but **never resolves**: destructive actions require the exact id |
| `status` no id | full dump (unbounded) | running jobs in full + last 20 exited + counts; `all: true` restores the full dump |
| registry growth | unbounded | **second tier**: cap retained exited entries (config, LRU by settle time; logs stay on disk); post-GC exact-id `output` falls back to the on-disk log |

**Invariant: resolution is read-only.** `output`/`status` may act on a resolved near-miss; `stop` never kills a guessed id.

**Tiering:** rows 1–5 are **core** (this card); registry GC is **second tier** (opt-in config, follow-up friendly); the excluded list below is **excluded** with rationale.

### Security threat model

- **Attacker-controlled inputs:** job **command strings** and **log content**. Logs are written to `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log` and read back **raw** by `tail()` — on-disk bytes are NOT redacted — and both flow into `status` lines and `output` tails. Resolution therefore must not surface MORE attacker-controlled text than today's exact-id path: same tail budget, same `_shellJobStatusLine` shape. Resolution changes routing, not volume.
- **Id-enumeration side-channel:** the ≤3 closest-ids candidate list is a minor enumeration aid. Job ids are session-local and not secrets — accepted risk, stated here rather than hidden; no rate-limiting.
- **Instruction hierarchy / destructive gate:** a typo'd or prompt-injected `bash_job stop` must never kill a job the caller did not name exactly. `stop` never acts on a resolved id (AC5) — only the exact id authorizes a destructive verb; resolution is hygiene, the exact-id requirement is the boundary.
- **Impossible by construction:** resolution never fabricates log content — it returns `tail()` of a retained entry's real file, or the same clean error as today (E2).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — `output` with a near-miss id (same `sh-NNNN-` prefix, wrong suffix, exactly one retained match) returns the resolved job's tail, names the corrected id, and states it already exited. (IT, fake registry/env; E2E-1)
- **AC2** — unresolvable unknown id returns a NON-error result with ≤3 closest ids and an explicit do-not-retry note. (IT)
- **AC3** — `status` no-id output line count = running + min(exited, 20) + summary, verified as a property over registries with 0/100/10k exited jobs. (UT/IT; E2E-2)
- **AC4** — after GC prunes an exited entry, exact-id `output` still returns the tail from the on-disk log while the log exists; deleted log degrades to today's clean error. (IT)
- **AC5** — `stop` never acts on a resolved near-miss id (asserted: no kill call, hint returned). (IT)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1447
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1447
- **Title**: gh-1438 bash_job: resolve near-miss/stale job ids instead of 'unknown background job' dead-ends bound status output GC exited jobs
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1438` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +1487
- **Deletions**: -39
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T11:53:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T13:01:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #1438
### What changed

`bash_job` no longer dead-ends on stale or near-miss job ids: an unknown id resolves to its closest retained job (read actions only), the no-id `status` listing is bounded, and the registry GCs exited entries (gh-1438).

### Key decisions

- **Pure resolution core** — new `lib/src/tools/job_id_resolution.dart`: id-shape parse (`sh-<n>-<tail>`), prefix match, edit-distance closeness, `matchShellJobId` (unique / ambiguous / closest-≤3). The registry maps matches onto entries (`ShellJobLookup` sealed types); the tool layer renders messages.
- **Resolution is read-only** — `output`/`status` act on a unique `sh-<n>-` near-miss (tail + corrected id + "stop polling the stale id"); `stop` never kills a guessed id, it only hints the closest ids (AC5). Malformed ids (`sh-99`, no tail) skip resolution and keep today's shortest error (E3, REG-green).
- **Bounded status** — no-id `status` = running jobs + last 20 exited (newest settle first) + a counts line; `all: true` restores the full dump (AC3, property-tested over 0/100/10k exited jobs).
- **Exited-entry GC** — `ShellJobRegistry(maxRetainedExitedJobs: 100)`: oldest-settled pruned LRU, log files stay on disk, a tombstone map lets exact-id `output` fall back to the on-disk log (AC4); deleted log degrades to the clean error (E2).
- **Settle stamps** — `ShellJobEntry.settledAt` (first observation wins) drives GC order and the new "exited Nm ago" context on exact-id results.
- **Schema kept budget-neutral** — the over-window guard prices every schema character (`estimateRequestOverheadTokens`, chars/4) against the model window, and `agent_cli_headless_over_window_test` sits ~25 tokens under the edge: the expanded `bash_job` schema tipped request 1 over (4 requests instead of 2). Final wording is compressed to near merge-base parity; semantics live in the runtime messages.
- The `jobs:` yaml knob was deliberately not added (its `0 = disabled` convention clashes with the registry's `0 = prune-all`); hosts configure via the constructor.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/tools/job_id_resolution_test.dart test/tools/shell_jobs_test.dart test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart
dart test test/cli/agent_cli_headless_over_window_test.dart   # schema-overhead budget guard

# gh-1438: [WIP][GOAL] bash_job id-churn hardening — near-miss resolution, bounded status, exited-job GC

## Description

## Goal — bash_job id-churn hardening (v2, repair edit: mechanism + amplification + retracted framings + threat model + E2E layer; line numbers re-pinned)

One sentence: **`bash_job` becomes forgiving of stale and near-miss job ids** — an unknown id resolves to its closest retained job instead of dead-ending, and the tool's outputs stay bounded.

Observed in production (chief session, ~13h of monitor shifts): the agent re-polled job ids reconstructed from memory (correct `sh-NNNN-` numeric part, wrong hash suffix) — every poll returned a bare `unknown background job` error with zero recovery information, so the poll-per-turn loop survived for hundreds of turns. Separately, `bash_job status` with no id dumped 1600+ lines of exited jobs into the agent context.

## Why this framing

- ~~"Agent discipline problem — fix via prompt."~~ **RETRACTED.** The harness must be robust to imperfect id recall; a prompt-side "don't poll stale ids" fix depends on exactly the faculty that failed (memory reconstruction across hundreds of turns).
- ~~"Registry reaps finished jobs while notices still reference them."~~ **RETRACTED by evidence:** `_jobs` is grow-only — all ~1600 exited jobs were retained with their logs; the polled ids were **near-misses** (correct `sh-NNNN-` numeric part, wrong hash suffix), never reaped ids.
- ~~"Deduplicate settle notices."~~ **RETRACTED:** the notice path already carries suppression (`suppressSettleNotification`, lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:119; call site builtin_tools_bash.dart:490 — #562 shipped it). The loop was **poll-side**, not notice-side.

### Mechanism (falsifiable, step-1 form)

Settle wake arrives with the job id as free text → the agent answers `bash_job(output)` with an id reconstructed from memory → `job(id)` is an exact-match lookup over retained entries (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:215), so a one-char-wrong id is **indistinguishable from one that never existed** → the verb dead-ends in `StateError('unknown background job: $id')` (builtin_tools_bash.dart:586 / :606, shell_jobs.dart:300) with **zero recovery signal** — no near-miss candidates, no "exited Nm ago", no log-dir hint → each settle wake re-arms the same wrong poll.

### Why it survived ~13h / hundreds of turns (amplification)

The dead-end error is terminal and information-free: nothing in the result tells the agent to stop, re-derive, or look in `.fah/bash_jobs/`, so nothing breaks the loop from the tool side. Every iteration is answered with a competent one-line "routine" reply, which masks the loop in the transcript as normal task discharge — hours of successful-looking execution outweigh any lost instruction (self-precedent). And the agent's periodic no-id `bash_job status` flooded context with 1600+ exited-job status lines (observed live), burying the correct id under noise and further degrading id fidelity on the next reconstruction.

## Pinned facts (current code — verified against the working tree, this edit)

- `ShellJobRegistry._jobs` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:199) is a grow-only list — exited jobs are retained for the process lifetime with their logs; there is no GC and no cap. (pos: AC3 bounding holds over 0/100/10k retained; neg: current unbounded dump is the REG baseline)
- Exact-match lookup `ShellJobEntry? job(String id)` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:215) returns null on any mismatch. (pos: AC1 near-miss resolution; neg: E3 non-`sh-NNNN-` shape skips resolution)
- Unknown ids throw `StateError('unknown background job: $id')` from three verb paths: builtin_tools_bash.dart:586 (`status`), :606 (`stop`), shell_jobs.dart:300 (`tail`, used by `output`). (pos: AC2 non-error recovery result; neg: E2 clean error after GC+log deletion)
- `tail()` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:297) reads the job's log file raw. (pos: AC1 resolved tail; neg: E2 deleted-log degradation)
- `_bashJobStatusResult` (builtin_tools_bash.dart:576) with no id maps every retained entry 1:1 via `jobs.jobs.map(_shellJobStatusLine).join('\n')` — unbounded by construction. (pos: AC3 bounded rendering; neg: `all: true` opt-out still restores the full dump)
- Logs persist under `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log` and remain readable after exit; on-disk content is NOT redacted (see threat model).
- Retraction evidence: notice suppression exists — `suppressSettleNotification` (lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart:119, called at builtin_tools_bash.dart:490).

## Capability surface (bash_job call shapes → behavior)

| call | today | becomes |
|---|---|---|
| `output`/`status` exact id, live or exited | works (tail from log) | unchanged, plus "exited Nm ago" context |
| `output` unknown id, unique `sh-NNNN-` prefix match among retained jobs | error dead-end | resolve: return that job's tail + corrected id + "already exited — stop polling the stale id" |
| `output`/`status` unknown id, ambiguous or no match | bare error | plain result listing up to 3 closest retained ids + "this id was never registered; do not retry" |
| `stop` unknown id | error dead-end | same closest-ids hint, but **never resolves**: destructive actions require the exact id |
| `status` no id | full dump (unbounded) | running jobs in full + last 20 exited + counts; `all: true` restores the full dump |
| registry growth | unbounded | **second tier**: cap retained exited entries (config, LRU by settle time; logs stay on disk); post-GC exact-id `output` falls back to the on-disk log |

**Invariant: resolution is read-only.** `output`/`status` may act on a resolved near-miss; `stop` never kills a guessed id.

**Tiering:** rows 1–5 are **core** (this card); registry GC is **second tier** (opt-in config, follow-up friendly); the excluded list below is **excluded** with rationale.

### Security threat model

- **Attacker-controlled inputs:** job **command strings** and **log content**. Logs are written to `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log` and read back **raw** by `tail()` — on-disk bytes are NOT redacted — and both flow into `status` lines and `output` tails. Resolution therefore must not surface MORE attacker-controlled text than today's exact-id path: same tail budget, same `_shellJobStatusLine` shape. Resolution changes routing, not volume.
- **Id-enumeration side-channel:** the ≤3 closest-ids candidate list is a minor enumeration aid. Job ids are session-local and not secrets — accepted risk, stated here rather than hidden; no rate-limiting.
- **Instruction hierarchy / destructive gate:** a typo'd or prompt-injected `bash_job stop` must never kill a job the caller did not name exactly. `stop` never acts on a resolved id (AC5) — only the exact id authorizes a destructive verb; resolution is hygiene, the exact-id requirement is the boundary.
- **Impossible by construction:** resolution never fabricates log content — it returns `tail()` of a retained entry's real file, or the same clean error as today (E2).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — `output` with a near-miss id (same `sh-NNNN-` prefix, wrong suffix, exactly one retained match) returns the resolved job's tail, names the corrected id, and states it already exited. (IT, fake registry/env; E2E-1)
- **AC2** — unresolvable unknown id returns a NON-error result with ≤3 closest ids and an explicit do-not-retry note. (IT)
- **AC3** — `status` no-id output line count = running + min(exited, 20) + summary, verified as a property over registries with 0/100/10k exited jobs. (UT/IT; E2E-2)
- **AC4** — after GC prunes an exited entry, exact-id `output` still returns the tail from the on-disk log while the log exists; deleted log degrades to today's clean error. (IT)
- **AC5** — `stop` never acts on a resolved near-miss id (asserted: no kill call, hint returned). (IT)

## Test plan

### Test matrix — maximal coverage, layered UT/IT/E2E/REG

- `UT-*` pure id-distance/prefix resolution + status-bounding math (AC1/AC3).
- `IT-*` fake `ExecutionEnv` registry: near-miss unique/ambiguous/exact, GC'd-with-log, malformed id (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5).
- `E2E-*` real-host PTY suites — the repo's existing seam for background jobs is the integration PTY family that drives R…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1447
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1447
- **Title**: gh-1438 bash_job: resolve near-miss/stale job ids instead of 'unknown background job' dead-ends bound status output GC exited jobs
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1438` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 9
- **Additions**: +1487
- **Deletions**: -39
- **Created**: 2026-10-09T11:53:44Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-09T13:01:37Z

## PR Description

Closes #1438
### What changed

`bash_job` no longer dead-ends on stale or near-miss job ids: an unknown id resolves to its closest retained job (read actions only), the no-id `status` listing is bounded, and the registry GCs exited entries (gh-1438).

### Key decisions

- **Pure resolution core** — new `lib/src/tools/job_id_resolution.dart`: id-shape parse (`sh-<n>-<tail>`), prefix match, edit-distance closeness, `matchShellJobId` (unique / ambiguous / closest-≤3). The registry maps matches onto entries (`ShellJobLookup` sealed types); the tool layer renders messages.
- **Resolution is read-only** — `output`/`status` act on a unique `sh-<n>-` near-miss (tail + corrected id + "stop polling the stale id"); `stop` never kills a guessed id, it only hints the closest ids (AC5). Malformed ids (`sh-99`, no tail) skip resolution and keep today's shortest error (E3, REG-green).
- **Bounded status** — no-id `status` = running jobs + last 20 exited (newest settle first) + a counts line; `all: true` restores the full dump (AC3, property-tested over 0/100/10k exited jobs).
- **Exited-entry GC** — `ShellJobRegistry(maxRetainedExitedJobs: 100)`: oldest-settled pruned LRU, log files stay on disk, a tombstone map lets exact-id `output` fall back to the on-disk log (AC4); deleted log degrades to the clean error (E2).
- **Settle stamps** — `ShellJobEntry.settledAt` (first observation wins) drives GC order and the new "exited Nm ago" context on exact-id results.
- **Schema kept budget-neutral** — the over-window guard prices every schema character (`estimateRequestOverheadTokens`, chars/4) against the model window, and `agent_cli_headless_over_window_test` sits ~25 tokens under the edge: the expanded `bash_job` schema tipped request 1 over (4 requests instead of 2). Final wording is compressed to near merge-base parity; semantics live in the runtime messages.
- The `jobs:` yaml knob was deliberately not added (its `0 = disabled` convention clashes with the registry's `0 = prune-all`); hosts configure via the constructor.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/tools/job_id_resolution_test.dart test/tools/shell_jobs_test.dart test/tools/bash_job_resolution_test.dart
dart test test/cli/agent_cli_headless_over_window_test.dart   # schema-overhead budget guard
dart test --exclude-tags integration                           # full gate, 9.8k tests
```

<details><summary>Resolution flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  REQ[bash_job output/status id] --> LK{registry.lookup}
  LK -->|exact| HIT[tail + exited-Nm-ago context]
  LK|unique sh-n- prefix| NM[tail + corrected id + stop-polling note]
  LK|2+ share prefix| AMB[list candidates, no pick E1]
  LK|none| UNK{shape + GC tombstone}
  UNK|malformed| ERR[shortest error E3]
  UNK|pruned| DISK[tail from on-disk log AC4 / clean error E2]
  UNK|never registered| HINT[≤3 closest ids + do-not-retry AC2]

```
