- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer
  functions (registered/path/vendor/prefix/pem/asn1/connection/context/
  entropy/pii) merged priority-first into `RedactionPipeline.scan/redact`
  with `[REDACTED:<kind>]` idempotent markers, allowlist + data-URL
  pass-through, live-mutable `RedactionConfig`, and `RedactionStats`
  (per layer + per tool). `redaction_hooks.dart` attaches it to the agent:
  afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext
  masks the outgoing context, beforeToolCall denies credential-file
  read/bash in `blockMode`, `redactPrompt` masks user input — write-side
  tools (`write`/`edit`/`checkpoint`/MCP write-ish) are never filtered
  (AC7). Config: `redact:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project
  `.fah/config.yaml` (tolerant parse). CLI `/redact`; docs/redaction.md.
- `lib/src/hashline/` — hashline patch language: `[path#TAG]` headers
  (4-hex xxHash32 of whole file), `SWAP`/`DEL`/`INS.*` ops, all-or-nothing
  `HashlinePatcher`, stale tags reject before any write. Wired in
  `builtin_tools.dart`: `edit` takes `patch`, `read` takes `hashline` flag.
- `lib/src/tools/read_selector.dart` — `read` trailing selectors:
  `:N`/`:A-B`/`:A+C` (`..` alias), comma multi-ranges, `:raw`. A literal
  file named `x:1-2` wins over the selector. `offset`/`limit` must not be
  combined with a selector.
- `lib/src/tools/archive_reader.dart` — `read` inside archives
  (`a.zip:inner/entry`, `.tar`, `.tgz`), 256 MiB cap.
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/` — `read` SQLite targets (`db.sqlite`,
  `:table[:key][?params]`, `?q=SELECT`). FFI engine (`package:sqlite3`)
  exported only from `lib/io.dart`, passed via `builtinTools(env, sqlite:)`;
  without it a clean "not supported" note.
- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — background shell jobs:
  `ShellJobRegistry` over the `BackgroundShell` capability
  (`execution_env.dart`; `LocalShell`/`LocalExecutionEnv` implement it,
  `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`/`SecretsExecutionEnv`/`MemoryExecutionEnv` and
  the app's `ProjectMountEnv`/`SandboxedExecutionEnv`/
  `PersistentWebExecutionEnv` forward it — the desktop app runs the host
  shell; mobile's `WasiSandboxShell` and web's `MemoryShell` run jobs as
  detached script Futures on job-local interpreter clones via
  `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/shell_job.dart` — own cwd/vars/capture, shared
  fs). `bash background: true` runs detached with output
  streaming into `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log`; `bash_job {status|output|stop}`
  (write tier) manages them. A settle fires `onSettled` on every exit —
  the CLI's terminal bookkeeping (`_onShellJobSettled`: job-board Running
  count, waiting row) hangs off it (issue #562). The model-facing notice
  (steered mid-run or a fresh idle turn; app `sendText` system-notice)
  is skipped when a foreground call consumed the result inline
  (`suppressSettleNotification`). Job logs on disk are NOT secret-redacted.
- `lib/src/tools/availability.dart` + `availability_gate.dart` —
  capability-gated tool availability (issue #19): `resolveToolAvailability`
  merges the `tools:` scope stack (global `~/.fah/config.yaml` < project
  `.fah/config.yaml` < session `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml` < runtime
  `--tools`/`FA_TOOLS`; deepest scope wins per key) over the host's hard
  capability floor — absent tools can never be force-enabled, unknown ids
  warn. The gate applies a resolution to the live registry idempotently
  (hide/restore + prompt rebuild) and tombstones calls to disabled tools.
  CLI surface in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_tools.dart` (`/tools`, live
  rebuild); docs/tool-availability.md is the user-facing page.
- `lib/src/tools/load_modes.dart` + `discover_tools_tool.dart` — agent
  load modes (issue #680): `--omp` > `FA_AGENT_MODE` > `agent.mode`
  (`default|pi|omp`) pick the tool-LOAD preset — `default` loads every
  enabled tool; `pi` the 4-tool benchmark base (issue #679, discovery
  off); `omp` the essential base with everything else discoverable,
  mounted on demand through the omp-only `discover_tools` meta tool (an
  explicit `tools: {id: on}` is a standing mount). The gate's
  `discoveryEnabled` flag keeps the discoverable tombstone from
  dead-ending on `discover_tools` in modes that don't register it. CLI
  sync + `/settings` switch in `agent_cli_tools.dart`/`settings_flow.dart`;
  user-facing docs: docs/tool-availability.md §Load modes.
- `lib/src/lsp/` — `lsp` tool (diagnostics/definition/references/rename):
  pure-Dart JSON-RPC client over `LspTransport`; `.dart` →
  `dart language-server --protocol=lsp`, projects merge `.fah/lsp.json`;
  lazy start, 5-min idle shutdown, crash respawn with backoff; renames apply
  all-or-nothing through the env. IO transport only via `lib/io.dart` +
  `builtinTools(env, lsp:)`; 1-indexed line/character; missing server =
  clean note, never a crash.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

1. **`lookup` resolution and GC tombstones:** `ShellJobRegistry.lookup(id)` classifies against `_jobs` only — GC'd ids map to `ShellJobUnknownId` with closest retained ids. The tool layer handles `prunedLogPath` in `_unknownOutputResult`, `_statusUnknownText`/`_gcStatusNote`, and `_bashJobStopResult`. OK.

2. **Potential bug in `_statusUnknownText`:** In `_bashJobStatusResult`:
```dart
ShellJobUnknownId(:final closestIds) => ToolExecutionResult.text(
  _unknownIdText(
    jobs,
    lookup.id,
    closestIds,
    gcNote: _statusUnknownText(jobs, lookup.id, closestIds),
  ),
```
`_statusUnknownText` returns `_unknownIdText(jobs, id, closestIds, gcNote: _gcStatusNote(jobs, id))` — then the outer `_unknownIdText` is invoked with `gcNote` already being the full text; `_unknownIdText` returns gcNote directly if non-null. This works but is convoluted — a double-wrapping: `_unknownIdText(gcNote: _unknownIdText(gcNote: ...))`. It's redundant but functionally correct. Style/complexity issue → SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT.

Wait, actually there's a subtle behavior: for a malformed id, `_statusUnknownText` throws StateError — that preserves E3. OK.

3. **`_unknownOutputResult` behavior for a GC'd id whose parse succeeds:** returns tail from log. Note: `tail.isEmpty ? '(no output)' : tail`. Fine.

4. **Potential real bug — `shellJobIdCloseness` and prefix matching with different n values:** `matchShellJobId` only resolves when the numeric part `n` matches exactly. If the agent misrembers the numeric part (e.g., `sh-1042-` vs `sh-1014-`), it falls to `ShellJobIdNoMatch` with closest ids. Fine per spec.

5. **`_editDistance` DP correctness:** Standard double-row Levenshtein. `current[0] = i + 1` — correct. Swap at end. Return previous[b.length]. Correct.

Wait — there's a subtle issue: after the loop, `previous` holds row for i=a.length. Correct.

6. **`parseShellJobIdParts` regex: `^sh-(\d*)-(.*)$`** — This parses `sh--foo` (empty n)? `\d*` allows empty, so `sh--abc` → n='' → int.tryParse('') → null → return null. OK malformed.

`sh-1-` → tail empty → return null. So `sh-1-` (dash but empty tail) is malformed. Hmm — but a real id always has non-empty tail. `sh-1` doesn't match at all (no second dash). OK.

Edge: `sh-001-x` → n=1 via int.tryParse → matches numeric part 1. So `sh-001-xyz` would resolve to job `sh-1-...`. That's arguably fine (same n).

But wait — there's a subtle issue: what if the job id is `sh-12-abc` and the requested is `sh-1-2abc`? Requested n=1, no match with n=12. No resolution — closest ids listed. Fine.

7. **A near-miss resolving to the WRONG job:** The scenario: agent polled `sh-7-wrongtail` but job `sh-7-...` from a DIFFERENT process shares workspace... Job ids are session-local, and registry is session-local. Multiple processes share a workspace but not a registry. OK.

But here's a more interesting scenario: jobs `sh-3-aaa` exited and GC'd (pruned), then job `sh-3-bbb`... wait, `_nextId` is per-registry monotonic, so each n is unique per registry. Two retained jobs can share n only if... actually `newShellJobId(_nextId++)` — n strictly increases per registry. So two entries can NEVER share the same n within one registry! The ambiguous case (E1) can only arise from... hmm, the test uses `env.forcedIds = ['sh-1-aaa', 'sh-1-bbb']` to force it. So in production the ambiguity case never happens (each n is unique). It's defensive. Fine — not a bug, but the ambiguity path is dead code in production. Not worth flagging beyond a suggestion-level note... Actually wait — is it truly impossible? `ShellJobRegistry.start` mints ids with `_nextId++`. Yes, unique n per registry. The E1 path is only reachable via manually-constructed ids. It's harmless defensiveness.

8. **GC bug — `_gcExitedJobs` tombstone loop:**
```dart
final pruneIds = {for (var i = 0; i < overflow; i++) exited[order[i]].id};
_jobs.removeWhere((entry) => pruneIds.contains(entry.id));
for (final entry in exited) {
```

This works. But note: `_prunedLogPaths` grows unboundedly across a session (one entry per pruned job). With thousands of jobs, it holds id+path strings — bounded by total jobs ever, small strings. Acceptable; documented ("cheap enough to keep for the session").

9. **GC ordering bug — LRU claim:** Docs say "oldest-settled pruned LRU". It's prune-oldest-settled, which is FIFO by settle time, not LRU (no touch-based recency). Naming nit. Not a real bug.

10. **Real issue — settle stamp race for the "exited Nm ago" on status lines:** `entry._settledAt ??= DateTime.now()` in the settle listener. 11. **Bigger issue — `_bySettledDescending` with null settledAt sorts to the end (epoch).** OK as documented.

12. **`_gcExitedJobs` runs on every settle and is O(n log n) over all exited entries.** With maxRetained 100 and thousands of jobs, each settle triggers a rebuild of the exited list (~100+overflow entries) — the list is capped at ~101 entries after GC (well, exited ≤ 100 + 1 new). Wait — actually there's a subtle issue: `_gcExitedJobs` computes `overflow = exited.length - maxRetainedExitedJobs`. 17. **AC3 line-count property:** lines = running + min(exited,20) + (1 summary line if truncated). The ticket says "status no-id output line count = running + min(exited, 20) + summary". Implementation matches.

18. **Potential correctness issue in `_bashJobStatusResult` bounded listing:** it sorts exited by `_bySettledDescending`, but `shown` uses `exited.take(_statusExitedLimit)`. The "…" line is only added when exited.length > 20. OK.

blocks.text:
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer
  functions (registered/path/vendor/prefix/pem/asn1/connection/context/
  entropy/pii) merged priority-first into `RedactionPipeline.scan/redact`
  with `[REDACTED:<kind>]` idempotent markers, allowlist + data-URL
  pass-through, live-mutable `RedactionConfig`, and `RedactionStats`
  (per layer + per tool). `redaction_hooks.dart` attaches it to the agent:
  afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext
  masks the outgoing context, beforeToolCall denies credential-file
  read/bash in `blockMode`, `redactPrompt` masks user input — write-side
  tools (`write`/`edit`/`checkpoint`/MCP write-ish) are never filtered
  (AC7). Config: `redact:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project
  `.fah/config.yaml` (tolerant parse). CLI `/redact`; docs/redaction.md.
- `lib/src/hashline/` — hashline patch language: `[path#TAG]` headers
  (4-hex xxHash32 of whole file), `SWAP`/`DEL`/`INS.*` ops, all-or-nothing
  `HashlinePatcher`, stale tags reject before any write. Wired in
  `builtin_tools.dart`: `edit` takes `patch`, `read` takes `hashline` flag.
- `lib/src/tools/read_selector.dart` — `read` trailing selectors:
  `:N`/`:A-B`/`:A+C` (`..` alias), comma multi-ranges, `:raw`. A literal
  file named `x:1-2` wins over the selector. `offset`/`limit` must not be
  combined with a selector.
- `lib/src/tools/archive_reader.dart` — `read` inside archives
  (`a.zip:inner/entry`, `.tar`, `.tgz`), 256 MiB cap.
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/` — `read` SQLite targets (`db.sqlite`,
  `:table[:key][?params]`, `?q=SELECT`). FFI engine (`package:sqlite3`)
  exported only from `lib/io.dart`, passed via `builtinTools(env, sqlite:)`;
  without it a clean "not supported" note.
- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — background shell jobs:
  `ShellJobRegistry` over the `BackgroundShell` capability
  (`execution_env.dart`; `LocalShell`/`LocalExecutionEnv` implement it,
  `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`/`SecretsExecutionEnv`/`MemoryExecutionEnv` and
  the app's `ProjectMountEnv`/`SandboxedExecutionEnv`/
  `PersistentWebExecutionEnv` forward it — the desktop app runs the host
  shell; mobile's `WasiSandboxShell` and web's `MemoryShell` run jobs as
  detached script Futures on job-local interpreter clones via
  `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/shell_job.dart` — own cwd/vars/capture, shared
  fs). `bash background: true` runs detached with output
  streaming into `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log`; `bash_job {status|output|stop}`
  (write tier) manages them. A settle fires `onSettled` on every exit —
  the CLI's terminal bookkeeping (`_onShellJobSettled`: job-board Running
  count, waiting row) hangs off it (issue #562). The model-facing notice
  (steered mid-run or a fresh idle turn; app `sendText` system-notice)
  is skipped when a foreground call consumed the result inline
  (`suppressSettleNotification`). Job logs on disk are NOT secret-redacted.
- `lib/src/tools/availability.dart` + `availability_gate.dart` —
  capability-gated tool availability (issue #19): `resolveToolAvailability`
  merges the `tools:` scope stack (global `~/.fah/config.yaml` < project
  `.fah/config.yaml` < session `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml` < runtime
  `--tools`/`FA_TOOLS`; deepest scope wins per key) over the host's hard
  capability floor — absent tools can never be force-enabled, unknown ids
  warn. The gate applies a resolution to the live registry idempotently
  (hide/restore + prompt rebuild) and tombstones calls to disabled tools.
  CLI surface in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_tools.dart` (`/tools`, live
  rebuild); docs/tool-availability.md is the user-facing page.
- `lib/src/tools/load_modes.dart` + `discover_tools_tool.dart` — agent
  load modes (issue #680): `--omp` > `FA_AGENT_MODE` > `agent.mode`
  (`default|pi|omp`) pick the tool-LOAD preset — `default` loads every

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
===

  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer
  functions (registered/path/vendor/prefix/pem/asn1/connection/context/
  entropy/pii) merged priority-first into `RedactionPipeline.scan/redact`
  with `[REDACTED:<kind>]` idempotent markers, allowlist + data-URL
  pass-through, live-mutable `RedactionConfig`, and `RedactionStats`
  (per layer + per tool). `redaction_hooks.dart` attaches it to the agent:
  afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext
  masks the outgoing context, beforeToolCall denies credential-file
  read/bash in `blockMode`, `redactPrompt` masks user input — write-side
  tools (`write`/`edit`/`checkpoint`/MCP write-ish) are never filtered
  (AC7). Config: `redact:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project
  `.fah/config.yaml` (tolerant parse). CLI `/redact`; docs/redaction.md.
- `lib/src/hashline/` — hashline patch language: `[path#TAG]` headers
  (4-hex xxHash32 of whole file), `SWAP`/`DEL`/`INS.*` ops, all-or-nothing
  `HashlinePatcher`, stale tags reject before any write. Wired in
  `builtin_tools.dart`: `edit` takes `patch`, `read` takes `hashline` flag.
- `lib/src/tools/read_selector.dart` — `read` trailing selectors:
  `:N`/`:A-B`/`:A+C` (`..` alias), comma multi-ranges, `:raw`. A literal
  file named `x:1-2` wins over the selector. `offset`/`limit` must not be
  combined with a selector.
- `lib/src/tools/archive_reader.dart` — `read` inside archives
  (`a.zip:inner/entry`, `.tar`, `.tgz`), 256 MiB cap.
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/` — `read` SQLite targets (`db.sqlite`,
  `:table[:key][?params]`, `?q=SELECT`). FFI engine (`package:sqlite3`)
  exported only from `lib/io.dart`, passed via `builtinTools(env, sqlite:)`;
  without it a clean "not supported" note.
- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — background shell jobs:
  `ShellJobRegistry` over the `BackgroundShell` capability
  (`execution_env.dart`; `LocalShell`/`LocalExecutionEnv` implement it,
  `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`/`SecretsExecutionEnv`/`MemoryExecutionEnv` and
  the app's `ProjectMountEnv`/`SandboxedExecutionEnv`/
  `PersistentWebExecutionEnv` forward it — the desktop app runs the host
  shell; mobile's `WasiSandboxShell` and web's `MemoryShell` run jobs as
  detached script Futures on job-local interpreter clones via
  `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/shell_job.dart` — own cwd/vars/capture, shared
  fs). `bash background: true` runs detached with output
  streaming into `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log`; `bash_job {status|output|stop}`
  (write tier) manages them. A settle fires `onSettled` on every exit —
  the CLI's terminal bookkeeping (`_onShellJobSettled`: job-board Running
  count, waiting row) hangs off it (issue #562). The model-facing notice
  (steered mid-run or a fresh idle turn; app `sendText` system-notice)
  is skipped when a foreground call consumed the result inline
  (`suppressSettleNotification`). Job logs on disk are NOT secret-redacted.
- `lib/src/tools/availability.dart` + `availability_gate.dart` —
  capability-gated tool availability (issue #19): `resolveToolAvailability`
  merges the `tools:` scope stack (global `~/.fah/config.yaml` < project

  `--tools`/`FA_TOOLS`; deepest scope wins per key) over the host's hard
  capability floor — absent tools can never be force-enabled, unknown ids
  warn. The gate applies a resolution to the live registry idempotently
  (hide/restore + prompt rebuild) and tombstones calls to disabled tools.
  CLI surface in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_tools.dart` (`/tools`, live
  rebuild); docs/tool-availability.md is the user-facing page.
- `lib/src/tools/load_modes.dart` + `discover_tools_tool.dart` — agent
  load modes (issue #680): `--omp` > `FA_AGENT_MODE` > `agent.mode`

  enabled tool; `pi` the 4-tool benchmark base (issue #679, discovery
  off); `omp` the essential base with everything else discoverable,
  mounted on demand through the omp-only `discover_tools` meta tool (an
  explicit `tools: {id: on}` is a standing mount). The gate's
  `discoveryEnabled` flag keeps the discoverable tombstone from
  dead-ending on `discover_tools` in modes that don't register it. CLI
  sync + `/settings` switch in `agent_cli_tools.dart`/`settings_flow.dart`;

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
===

2. **Potential bug in `_statusUnknownText`:** In `_bashJobStatusResult`:

`_statusUnknownText` returns `_unknownIdText(jobs, id, closestIds, gcNote: _gcStatusNote(jobs, id))` — then the outer `_unknownIdText` is invoked with `gcNote` already being the full text; `_unknownIdText` returns gcNote directly if non-null. This works but is convoluted — a double-wrapping: `_unknownIdText(gcNote: _unknownIdText(gcNote: ...))`. It's redundant but functionally correct. Style/complexity issue → SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT.

Wait, actually there's a subtle behavior: for a malformed id, `_statusUnknownText` throws StateError — that preserves E3. OK.

3. **`_unknownOutputResult` behavior for a GC'd id whose parse succeeds:** returns tail from log. Note: `tail.isEmpty ? '(no output)' : tail`. Fine.

4. **Potential real bug — `shellJobIdCloseness` and prefix matching with different n values:** `matchShellJobId` only resolves when the numeric part `n` matches exactly. If the agent misrembers the numeric part (e.g., `sh-1042-` vs `sh-1014-`), it falls to `ShellJobIdNoMatch` with closest ids. Fine per spec.

5. **`_editDistance` DP correctness:** Standard double-row Levenshtein. `current[0] = i + 1` — correct. Swap at end. Return previous[b.length]. Correct.

Wait — there's a subtle issue: after the loop, `previous` holds row for i=a.length. Correct.

6. **`parseShellJobIdParts` regex: `^sh-(\d*)-(.*)$`** — This parses `sh--foo` (empty n)? `\d*` allows empty, so `sh--abc` → n='' → int.tryParse('') → null → return null. OK malformed.

`sh-1-` → tail empty → return null. So `sh-1-` (dash but empty tail) is malformed. Hmm — but a real id always has non-empty tail. `sh-1` doesn't match at all (no second dash). OK.

Edge: `sh-001-x` → n=1 via int.tryParse → matches numeric part 1. So `sh-001-xyz` would resolve to job `sh-1-...`. That's arguably fine (same n).

But wait — there's a subtle issue: what if the job id is `sh-12-abc` and the requested is `sh-1-2abc`? Requested n=1, no match with n=12. No resolution — closest ids listed. Fine.

7. **A near-miss resolving to the WRONG job:** The scenario: agent polled `sh-7-wrongtail` but job `sh-7-...` from a DIFFERENT process shares workspace... Job ids are session-local, and registry is session-local. Multiple processes share a workspace but not a registry. OK.

But here's a more interesting scenario: jobs `sh-3-aaa` exited and GC'd (pruned), then job `sh-3-bbb`... wait, `_nextId` is per-registry monotonic, so each n is unique per registry. Two retained jobs can share n only if... actually `newShellJobId(_nextId++)` — n strictly increases per registry. So two entries can NEVER share the same n within one registry! The ambiguous case (E1) can only arise from... hmm, the test uses `env.forcedIds = ['sh-1-aaa', 'sh-1-bbb']` to force it. So in production the ambiguity case never happens (each n is unique). It's defensive. Fine — not a bug, but the ambiguity path is dead code in production. Not worth flagging beyond a suggestion-level note... Actually wait — is it truly impossible? `ShellJobRegistry.start` mints ids with `_nextId++`. Yes, unique n per registry. The E1 path is only reachable via manually-constructed ids. It's harmless defensiveness.

8. **GC bug — `_gcExitedJobs` tombstone loop:**
```dart
final pruneIds = {for (var i = 0; i < overflow; i++) exited[order[i]].id};
_jobs.removeWhere((entry) => pruneIds.contains(entry.id));
for (final entry in exited) {

```
This works. But note: `_prunedLogPaths` grows unboundedly across a session (one entry per pruned job). With thousands of jobs, it holds id+path strings — bounded by total jobs ever, small strings. Acceptable; documented ("cheap enough to keep for the session").

9. **GC ordering bug — LRU claim:** Docs say "oldest-settled pruned LRU". It's prune-oldest-settled, which is FIFO by settle time, not LRU (no touch-based recency). Naming nit. Not a real bug.

10. **Real issue — settle stamp race for the "exited Nm ago" on status lines:** `entry._settledAt ??= DateTime.now()` in the settle listener. 11. **Bigger issue — `_bySettledDescending` with null settledAt sorts to the end (epoch).** OK as documented.

12. **`_gcExitedJobs` runs on every settle and is O(n log n) over all exited entries.** With maxRetained 100 and thousands of jobs, each settle triggers a rebuild of the exited list (~100+overflow entries) — the list is capped at ~101 entries after GC (well, exited ≤ 100 + 1 new). - `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer
  functions (registered/path/vendor/prefix/pem/asn1/connection/context/
  entropy/pii) merged priority-first into `RedactionPipeline.scan/redact`
  with `[REDACTED:<kind>]` idempotent markers, allowlist + data-URL
  pass-through, live-mutable `RedactionConfig`, and `RedactionStats`
  (per layer + per tool). `redaction_hooks.dart` attaches it to the agent:
  afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext
  masks the outgoing context, beforeToolCall denies credential-file
  read/bash in `blockMode`, `redactPrompt` masks user input — write-side
  tools (`write`/`edit`/`checkpoint`/MCP write-ish) are never filtered
  (AC7). Config: `redact:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project
  `.fah/config.yaml` (tolerant parse). CLI `/redact`; docs/redaction.md.
- `lib/src/hashline/` — hashline patch language: `[path#TAG]` headers
  (4-hex xxHash32 of whole file), `SWAP`/`DEL`/`INS.*` ops, all-or-nothing
  `HashlinePatcher`, stale tags reject before any write. Wired in
  `builtin_tools.dart`: `edit` takes `patch`, `read` takes `hashline` flag.
- `lib/src/tools/read_selector.dart` — `read` trailing selectors:
  `:N`/`:A-B`/`:A+C` (`..` alias), comma multi-ranges, `:raw`. A literal
  file named `x:1-2` wins over the selector. `offset`/`limit` must not be
  combined with a selector.
- `lib/src/tools/archive_reader.dart` — `read` inside archives
  (`a.zip:inner/entry`, `.tar`, `.tgz`), 256 MiB cap.
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/` — `read` SQLite targets (`db.sqlite`,
  `:table[:key][?params]`, `?q=SELECT`). FFI engine (`package:sqlite3`)
  exported only from `lib/io.dart`, passed via `builtinTools(env, sqlite:)`;
  without it a clean "not supported" note.
- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — background shell jobs:
  `ShellJobRegistry` over the `BackgroundShell` capability
  (`execution_env.dart`; `LocalShell`/`LocalExecutionEnv` implement it,
  `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`/`SecretsExecutionEnv`/`MemoryExecutionEnv` and
  the app's `ProjectMountEnv`/`SandboxedExecutionEnv`/
  `PersistentWebExecutionEnv` forward it — the desktop app runs the host
  shell; mobile's `WasiSandboxShell` and web's `MemoryShell` run jobs as
  detached script Futures on job-local interpreter clones via
  `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/shell_job.dart` — own cwd/vars/capture, shared
  fs). `bash background: true` runs detached with output
  streaming into `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log`; `bash_job {status|output|stop}`
  (write tier) manages them. A settle fires `onSettled` on every exit —
  the CLI's terminal bookkeeping (`_onShellJobSettled`: job-board Running
  count, waiting row) hangs off it (issue #562). The model-facing notice
  (steered mid-run or a fresh idle turn; app `sendText` system-notice)
  is skipped when a foreground call consumed the result inline
  (`suppressSettleNotification`). Job logs on disk are NOT secret-redacted.
- `lib/src/tools/availability.dart` + `availability_gate.dart` —
  capability-gated tool availability (issue #19): `resolveToolAvailability`
  merges the `tools:` scope stack (global `~/.fah/config.yaml` < project
  `.fah/config.yaml` < session `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml` < runtime
  `--tools`/`FA_TOOLS`; deepest scope wins per key) over the host's hard
  capability floor — absent tools can never be force-enabled, unknown ids
  warn. The gate applies a resolution to the live registry idempotently
  (hide/restore + prompt rebuild) and tombstones calls to disabled tools.
  CLI surface in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_tools.dart` (`/tools`, live
  rebuild); docs/tool-availability.md is the user-facing page.
- `lib/src/tools/load_modes.dart` + `discover_tools_tool.dart` — agent
  load modes (issue #680): `--omp` > `FA_AGENT_MODE` > `agent.mode`
  (`default|pi|omp`) pick the tool-LOAD preset — `default` loads every
  enabled tool; `pi` the 4-tool benchmark base (issue #679, discovery
  off); `omp` the essential base with everything else discoverable,
  mounted on demand through the omp-only `discover_tools` meta tool (an
  explicit `tools: {id: on}` is a standing mount). The gate's
  `discoveryEnabled` flag keeps the discoverable tombstone from
  dead-ending on `discover_tools` in modes that don't register it. CLI
  sync + `/settings` switch in `agent_cli_tools.dart`/`settings_flow.dart`;
  user-facing docs: docs/tool-availability.md §Load modes.
- `lib/src/lsp/` — `lsp` tool (diagnostics/definition/references/rename):
  pure-Dart JSON-RPC client over `LspTransport`; `.dart` →
  `dart language-server --protocol=lsp`, projects merge `.fah/lsp.json`;
  lazy start, 5-min idle shutdown, crash respawn with backoff; renames apply
  all-or-nothing through the env. IO transport only via `lib/io.dart` +
  `builtinTools(env, lsp:)`; 1-indexed line/character; missing server =
  clean note, never a crash.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
===

blocks.text:
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer
  functions (registered/path/vendor/prefix/pem/asn1/connection/context/
  entropy/pii) merged priority-first into `RedactionPipeline.scan/redact`
  with `[REDACTED:<kind>]` idempotent markers, allowlist + data-URL
  pass-through, live-mutable `RedactionConfig`, and `RedactionStats`
  (per layer + per tool). `redaction_hooks.dart` attaches it to the agent:
  afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext
  masks the outgoing context, beforeToolCall denies credential-file
  read/bash in `blockMode`, `redactPrompt` masks user input — write-side
  tools (`write`/`edit`/`checkpoint`/MCP write-ish) are never filtered
  (AC7). Config: `redact:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project
  `.fah/config.yaml` (tolerant parse). CLI `/redact`; docs/redaction.md.
- `lib/src/hashline/` — hashline patch language: `[path#TAG]` headers
  (4-hex xxHash32 of whole file), `SWAP`/`DEL`/`INS.*` ops, all-or-nothing
  `HashlinePatcher`, stale tags reject before any write. Wired in
  `builtin_tools.dart`: `edit` takes `patch`, `read` takes `hashline` flag.
- `lib/src/tools/read_selector.dart` — `read` trailing selectors:
  `:N`/`:A-B`/`:A+C` (`..` alias), comma multi-ranges, `:raw`. A literal
  file named `x:1-2` wins over the selector. `offset`/`limit` must not be
  combined with a selector.
- `lib/src/tools/archive_reader.dart` — `read` inside archives
  (`a.zip:inner/entry`, `.tar`, `.tgz`), 256 MiB cap.
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/` — `read` SQLite targets (`db.sqlite`,
  `:table[:key][?params]`, `?q=SELECT`). FFI engine (`package:sqlite3`)
  exported only from `lib/io.dart`, passed via `builtinTools(env, sqlite:)`;
  without it a clean "not supported" note.
- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — background shell jobs:
  `ShellJobRegistry` over the `BackgroundShell` capability
  (`execution_env.dart`; `LocalShell`/`LocalExecutionEnv` implement it,
  `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`/`SecretsExecutionEnv`/`MemoryExecutionEnv` and
  the app's `ProjectMountEnv`/`SandboxedExecutionEnv`/
  `PersistentWebExecutionEnv` forward it — the desktop app runs the host
  shell; mobile's `WasiSandboxShell` and web's `MemoryShell` run jobs as
  detached script Futures on job-local interpreter clones via
  `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/shell_job.dart` — own cwd/vars/capture, shared
  fs). `bash background: true` runs detached with output
  streaming into `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log`; `bash_job {status|output|stop}`
  (write tier) manages them. A settle fires `onSettled` on every exit —
  the CLI's terminal bookkeeping (`_onShellJobSettled`: job-board Running
  count, waiting row) hangs off it (issue #562). The model-facing notice
  (steered mid-run or a fresh idle turn; app `sendText` system-notice)
  is skipped when a foreground call consumed the result inline
  (`suppressSettleNotification`). Job logs on disk are NOT secret-redacted.
- `lib/src/tools/availability.dart` + `availability_gate.dart` —
  capability-gated tool availability (issue #19): `resolveToolAvailability`
  merges the `tools:` scope stack (global `~/.fah/config.yaml` < project
  `.fah/config.yaml` < session `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml` < runtime
  `--tools`/`FA_TOOLS`; deepest scope wins per key) over the host's hard
  capability floor — absent tools can never be force-enabled, unknown ids
  warn. The gate applies a resolution to the live registry idempotently
  (hide/restore + prompt rebuild) and tombstones calls to disabled tools.
  CLI surface in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_tools.dart` (`/tools`, live
  rebuild); docs/tool-availability.md is the user-facing page.
- `lib/src/tools/load_modes.dart` + `discover_tools_tool.dart` — agent
  load modes (issue #680): `--omp` > `FA_AGENT_MODE` > `agent.mode`
  (`default|pi|omp`) pick the tool-LOAD preset — `default` loads every
  enabled tool; `pi` the 4-tool benchmark base (issue #679, discovery
  off); `omp` the essential base with everything else discoverable,
  mounted on demand through the omp-only `discover_tools` meta tool (an

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
===

  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer
  functions (registered/path/vendor/prefix/pem/asn1/connection/context/
  entropy/pii) merged priority-first into `RedactionPipeline.scan/redact`
  with `[REDACTED:<kind>]` idempotent markers, allowlist + data-URL
  pass-through, live-mutable `RedactionConfig`, and `RedactionStats`
  (per layer + per tool). `redaction_hooks.dart` attaches it to the agent:
  afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext
  masks the outgoing context, beforeToolCall denies credential-file
  read/bash in `blockMode`, `redactPrompt` masks user input — write-side
  tools (`write`/`edit`/`checkpoint`/MCP write-ish) are never filtered
  (AC7). Config: `redact:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project
  `.fah/config.yaml` (tolerant parse). CLI `/redact`; docs/redaction.md.
- `lib/src/hashline/` — hashline patch language: `[path#TAG]` headers
  (4-hex xxHash32 of whole file), `SWAP`/`DEL`/`INS.*` ops, all-or-nothing
  `HashlinePatcher`, stale tags reject before any write. Wired in
  `builtin_tools.dart`: `edit` takes `patch`, `read` takes `hashline` flag.
- `lib/src/tools/read_selector.dart` — `read` trailing selectors:
  `:N`/`:A-B`/`:A+C` (`..` alias), comma multi-ranges, `:raw`. A literal
  file named `x:1-2` wins over the selector. `offset`/`limit` must not be
  combined with a selector.
- `lib/src/tools/archive_reader.dart` — `read` inside archives
  (`a.zip:inner/entry`, `.tar`, `.tgz`), 256 MiB cap.
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/` — `read` SQLite targets (`db.sqlite`,
  `:table[:key][?params]`, `?q=SELECT`). FFI engine (`package:sqlite3`)

  without it a clean "not supported" note.
- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — background shell jobs:
  `ShellJobRegistry` over the `BackgroundShell` capability
  (`execution_env.dart`; `LocalShell`/`LocalExecutionEnv` implement it,
  `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`/`SecretsExecutionEnv`/`MemoryExecutionEnv` and
  the app's `ProjectMountEnv`/`SandboxedExecutionEnv`/
  `PersistentWebExecutionEnv` forward it — the desktop app runs the host
  shell; mobile's `WasiSandboxShell` and web's `MemoryShell` run jobs as
  detached script Futures on job-local interpreter clones via

  fs). `bash background: true` runs detached with output

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

The ticket's capability-surface table lists "registry growth | unbounded | second tier: cap retained exited entries (config, LRU by settle time; logs stay on disk)". "opt-in config, follow-up friendly" suggested it might be deferred or behind a config. SUGGESTION-level note (or general comment). The PR description is upfront about it. I'll put it as a SUGGESTION inline on the default constant line: consider whether silent behavior change for existing embedders (flutter_app host now GCs) deserves an explicit note in AGENTS.md/docs — which folds into the AGENTS.md doc-gap finding.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
===

The gh-1438 test plan specifies two real-host PTY suites as part of the verification matrix:

- **E2E-2** (AC3) — pattern of `test/integration/job_board_stability_pty_test.dart`: with ~30 real exited jobs retained, no-id `status` keeps the transcript bounded and the board contract stays intact.

This PR ships only the UT layer (`job_id_resolution_test.dart`) and the IT layer (`shell_jobs_test.dart`, `bash_job_resolution_test.dart`) — both are good (AC1–AC5 and E1/E3 covered, including the over-window budget guard). But the E2E seam the ticket pinned ("the repo's existing seam for background jobs is the integration PTY family") is unverified: nothing exercises the new resolution/bounding through the live harness where the settle listener, real log files, and the job board run together.

Either add the two suites (they can be small — one real job + one stale poll for E2E-1) or record an explicit follow-up card in the PR description so the gap is tracked rather than silently dropped.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: AGENTS.md subsystem documentation is now stale**

AGENTS.md is this repo's convention source ("Keep it factual: paths, commands, invariants") and is updated by comparable subsystem PRs (gh-1412, gh-1395, fix(1408) all touched it). This PR changes the `shell_jobs` subsystem substantially but leaves its bullet stale:

- The `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` entry (line ~216) still describes the registry with no mention of: the exited-entry GC (`maxRetainedExitedJobs`, default 100, oldest-settled pruned, running jobs never pruned), the `_prunedLogPaths` tombstones + `tailFromLog` AC4 fallback, `ShellJobEntry.settledAt`, the `lookup()` sealed-type classification, or that no-id `bash_job status` is bounded to running + last 20 exited with `all: true` restoring the dump.
- The new subsystem file `lib/src/tools/job_id_resolution.dart` (this file) has no entry at all — the tools section lists every other `lib/src/tools/*` unit.

Please add/extend both bullets (the AC5 invariant is worth pinning there too: "resolution is read-only — `stop` never acts on a resolved id").

💡 **SUGGESTION: pin the `maxRetainedExitedJobs` contract (and note the default-on behavior change)**

```dart
this.maxRetainedExitedJobs = defaultMaxRetainedExitedJobs,
```

Two small things:

1. **No validation.** A negative value silently behaves as "prune all" (same as `0`: `overflow = exited.length - cap > 0` always). A one-line assert in the constructor initializer pins the contract: `assert(maxRetainedExitedJobs >= 0)`. The PR description itself notes the `0 = prune-all` semantics are surprising (`0 = disabled` is the yaml convention elsewhere) — an assert at least keeps negatives out.

2. **Default-on GC is a silent host behavior change.** The ticket tiered registry GC as *"second tier (opt-in config, follow-up friendly)"*, but this ships it default-on for every embedder — `ShellJobRegistry(env: …)` call sites in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:429` and `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart:780` now cap retention at 100 exited entries without any host-facing note. The PR description justifies the reasoning (the yaml `0`-convention clash), which is fair — but since no config knob exists, a line in AGENTS.md/docs (see the doc thread) is the only place a host learns its `bash_job status` listing now stops at 100 exited rows.

💡 **SUGGESTION: near-miss `output` re-scans the registry for a tail it can take from the entry in hand**

```dart
case ShellJobNearMiss(:final entry):
  final tail = await jobs.tail(entry.id, maxLines: maxLines);
```

`jobs.tail(id)` does another exact-match linear scan (`job(id)`) + unknown-id `StateError` path — for an entry this switch already holds. The sibling GC fallback path uses the direct file API; the same works here:

```dart
final content = await env.readTextFile(entry.logPath);
// or expose/keep a registry helper: tailFromLog(entry.logPath, maxLines: maxLines) ?? ''
```

Micro-scale (registries are capped at ~100), so this is tidy-as-you-go, not a perf fix — it just removes a redundant lookup and the unreachable throw branch.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: pin the `maxRetainedExitedJobs` contract (and note the default-on behavior change)**

```dart
this.maxRetainedExitedJobs = defaultMaxRetainedExitedJobs,
```

Two small things:

1. **No validation.** A negative value silently behaves as "prune all" (same as `0`: `overflow = exited.length - cap > 0` always). A one-line assert in the constructor initializer pins the contract: `assert(maxRetainedExitedJobs >= 0)`. The PR description itself notes the `0 = prune-all` semantics are surprising (`0 = disabled` is the yaml convention elsewhere) — an assert at least keeps negatives out.

2. **Default-on GC is a silent host behavior change.** The ticket tiered registry GC as *"second tier (opt-in config, follow-up friendly)"*, but this ships it default-on for every embedder — `ShellJobRegistry(env: …)` call sites in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:429` and `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart:780` now cap retention at 100 exited entries without any host-facing note. blocks.text:
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (issue #24): ten pure layer
  functions (registered/path/vendor/prefix/pem/asn1/connection/context/
  entropy/pii) merged priority-first into `RedactionPipeline.scan/redact`
  with `[REDACTED:<kind>]` idempotent markers, allowlist + data-URL
  pass-through, live-mutable `RedactionConfig`, and `RedactionStats`
  (per layer + per tool). `redaction_hooks.dart` attaches it to the agent:
  afterToolCall masks tool results BEFORE session persist, transformContext
  masks the outgoing context, beforeToolCall denies credential-file
  read/bash in `blockMode`, `redactPrompt` masks user input — write-side
  tools (`write`/`edit`/`checkpoint`/MCP write-ish) are never filtered
  (AC7). Config: `redact:` in `~/.fah/config.yaml` or project
  `.fah/config.yaml` (tolerant parse). CLI `/redact`; docs/redaction.md.
- `lib/src/hashline/` — hashline patch language: `[path#TAG]` headers
  (4-hex xxHash32 of whole file), `SWAP`/`DEL`/`INS.*` ops, all-or-nothing
  `HashlinePatcher`, stale tags reject before any write. Wired in
  `builtin_tools.dart`: `edit` takes `patch`, `read` takes `hashline` flag.
- `lib/src/tools/read_selector.dart` — `read` trailing selectors:
  `:N`/`:A-B`/`:A+C` (`..` alias), comma multi-ranges, `:raw`. A literal
  file named `x:1-2` wins over the selector. `offset`/`limit` must not be
  combined with a selector.
- `lib/src/tools/archive_reader.dart` — `read` inside archives
  (`a.zip:inner/entry`, `.tar`, `.tgz`), 256 MiB cap.
- `lib/src/tools/sqlite/` — `read` SQLite targets (`db.sqlite`,
  `:table[:key][?params]`, `?q=SELECT`). FFI engine (`package:sqlite3`)
  exported only from `lib/io.dart`, passed via `builtinTools(env, sqlite:)`;
  without it a clean "not supported" note.
- `lib/src/tools/shell_jobs.dart` — background shell jobs:
  `ShellJobRegistry` over the `BackgroundShell` capability
  (`execution_env.dart`; `LocalShell`/`LocalExecutionEnv` implement it,
  `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`/`SecretsExecutionEnv`/`MemoryExecutionEnv` and
  the app's `ProjectMountEnv`/`SandboxedExecutionEnv`/
  `PersistentWebExecutionEnv` forward it — the desktop app runs the host
  shell; mobile's `WasiSandboxShell` and web's `MemoryShell` run jobs as
  detached script Futures on job-local interpreter clones via
  `flutter_app/lib/sandbox/shell_job.dart` — own cwd/vars/capture, shared
  fs). `bash background: true` runs detached with output
  streaming into `.fah/bash_jobs/<id>.log`; `bash_job {status|output|stop}`
  (write tier) manages them. A settle fires `onSettled` on every exit —
  the CLI's terminal bookkeeping (`_onShellJobSettled`: job-board Running
  count, waiting row) hangs off it (issue #562). The model-facing notice
  (steered mid-run or a fresh idle turn; app `sendText` system-notice)
  is skipped when a foreground call consumed the result inline
  (`suppressSettleNotification`). Job logs on disk are NOT secret-redacted.
- `lib/src/tools/availability.dart` + `availability_gate.dart` —
  capability-gated tool availability (issue #19): `resolveToolAvailability`
  merges the `tools:` scope stack (global `~/.fah/config.yaml` < project
  `.fah/config.yaml` < session `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml` < runtime
  `--tools`/`FA_TOOLS`; deepest scope wins per key) over the host's hard
  capability floor — absent tools can never be force-enabled, unknown ids
  warn. The gate applies a resolution to the live registry idempotently
  (hide/restore + prompt rebuild) and tombstones calls to disabled tools.
  CLI surface in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_tools.dart` (`/tools`, live
  rebuild); docs/tool-availability.md is the user-facing page.
- `lib/src/tools/load_modes.dart` + `discover_tools_tool.dart` — agent
  load modes (issue #680): `--omp` > `FA_AGENT_MODE` > `agent.mode`
  (`default|pi|omp`) pick the tool-LOAD preset — `default` loads every
  enabled tool; `pi` the 4-tool benchmark base (issue #679, discovery
  off); `omp` the essential base with everything else discoverable,
  mounted on demand through the omp-only `discover_tools` meta tool (an
  explicit `tools: {id: on}` is a standing mount). The gate's
  `discoveryEnabled` flag keeps the discoverable tombstone from
  dead-ending on `discover_tools` in modes that don't register it. CLI
  sync + `/settings` switch in `agent_cli_tools.dart`/`settings_flow.dart`;
  user-facing docs: docs/tool-availability.md §Load modes.
- `lib/src/lsp/` — `lsp` tool (diagnostics/definition/references/rename):
  pure-Dart JSON-RPC client over `LspTransport`; `.dart` →
  `dart language-server --protocol=lsp`, projects merge `.fah/lsp.json`;
  lazy start, 5-min idle shutdown, crash respawn with backoff; renames apply
  all-or-nothing through the env. IO transport only via `lib/io.dart` +
  `builtinTools(env, lsp:)`; 1-indexed line/character; missing server =

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
===

```dart
this.maxRetainedExitedJobs = defaultMaxRetainedExitedJobs,
```

Two small things:

1. **No validation.** A negative value silently behaves as "prune all" (same as `0`: `overflow = exited.length - cap > 0` always). A one-line assert in the constructor initializer pins the contract: `assert(maxRetainedExitedJobs >= 0)`. The PR description itself notes the `0 = prune-all` semantics are surprising (`0 = disabled` is the yaml convention elsewhere) — an assert at least keeps negatives out.

2. **Default-on GC is a silent host behavior change.** The ticket tiered registry GC as *"second tier (opt-in config, follow-up friendly)"*, but this ships it default-on for every embedder — `ShellJobRegistry(env: …)` call sites in `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart:429` and `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart:780` now cap retention at 100 exited entries without any host-facing note. The PR description justifies the reasoning (the yaml `0`-convention clash), which is fair — but since no config knob exists, a line in AGENTS.md/docs (see the doc thread) is the only place a host learns its `bash_job status` listing now stops at 100 exited rows.
